title: Vice-President inaugurates Iconic Tower at Sri Sri University in Cuttack, says it symbolises the confluence of India’s rich cultural heritage and modern educational aspirations
subtitle:
India’s higher education sector has undergone a remarkable transformation in the past decade, with substantial growth in institutions and enrolment: Vice-President

Bharat must become strong and capable so that no one can dictate terms to it: Vice-President

Vice-President urges universities in Odisha to introduce School Connect programmes to prevent tribal student dropouts and promote inclusive education
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 NOV 2026 3:03PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the Iconic Tower at Sri Sri University in Cuttack, Odisha, in the presence of the Governor of Odisha, Shri Braj Mohan Ram; the Chief Minister of Odisha, Shri Mohan Charan Majhi; Gurudev Sri Sri Ravishankar, Founder and Lifetime President of Sri Sri University.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the magnificent Iconic Tower at Sri Sri University in Cuttack, Odisha.

Describing the Tower as a symbol of the confluence of India’s rich cultural heritage, timeless wisdom and modern educational aspirations, he emphasised the importance of education in nurturing knowledge, character and compassion towards building a Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

He also called upon universities in Odisha to introduce School Connect programmes to support tribal students and prevent dropouts.

Governor of Odisha, Shri Braj Mohan Ram; Chief Minister of Odisha, Shri Mohan Charan Majhi; Founder and Lifetime President, Sri Sri University, Gurudev Sri Sri Ravishankar; and President and Chairperson of the Board of Governors, Sri Sri University, Shri Aadesh Goyal were present on the occasion.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
November 16, 2026
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that the inauguration marked much more than the opening of a building, as it celebrated a vision, an inspiring philosophy of education, India’s glorious cultural inheritance and a commitment to shaping the future of Bharat.
Describing Sri Sri University as the manifestation of the remarkable vision of Gurudev Sri Sri Ravishankar, the Vice-President said that Gurudev’s understanding of education transcended the conventional boundaries of academic learning. He noted that the University, envisioned as a confluence of Eastern wisdom and Western knowledge, commenced its academic journey in 2012, with a founding philosophy that true education must nurture the character, consciousness and compassion of an individual. Emphasising the relevance of this vision in contemporary times, he said that education must prepare young people not only for academic success but also to contribute meaningfully to society and become responsible citizens of the world.
The Vice-President expressed happiness that Sri Sri University described itself as the “Happiest Campus in the World”, observing that happiness was something the entire humanity aspired for and that it was deeply rooted in India’s culture and traditions. He appreciated the University’s efforts in promoting these enduring cultural values.
Highlighting Odisha’s rich architectural and cultural heritage, the Vice-President said that architecture in the State had always represented much more than the construction of physical spaces, with its temples serving as enduring expressions of artistic excellence, scientific knowledge, spirituality and cultural continuity. Referring to the sacred Lord Jagannath Temple at Puri, the temples of Bhubaneswar and the grandeur of the Konark Temple, he said that the Kalinga architectural tradition bore testimony to the extraordinary creative genius of India’s civilisation.
The Vice-President observed that the Iconic Tower drew inspiration from this rich heritage, with its ascending form symbolising the journey of human aspiration from the foundations of knowledge towards the heights of wisdom and enlightenment.
Referring to the larger national aspirations, the Vice-President said that the Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, had given the country the inspiring vision of Viksit Bharat @2047, envisaging a developed India celebrating the centenary of its Independence with confidence, capability and global leadership. He said that the Prime Minister had repeatedly emphasised the transformative role of educational institutions in realising this national ambition.
Highlighting the expansion of higher education over the past twelve years, the Vice-President said that the number of universities in the country had increased from 760 in 2014-15 to more than 1,400 today. He noted that the number of Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) had increased from 16 before 2014 to 23, while the number of Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs) had grown from 13 to 22. He further stated that the number of All India Institutes of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) had increased from 7 before 2014 to 20, while student enrolment in higher education institutions had risen from 3.42 crore in 2014-15 to more than 4.50 crore.
Referring to Odisha’s sizeable tribal population, the Vice-President urged all universities in Odisha, both government and private, to introduce School Connect programmes for tribal children to ensure that they did not drop out of education and were encouraged to pursue higher studies.
Emphasising the importance of India’s cultural identity and national strength, the Vice-President said that Bharat’s culture and traditions had an important role to play in shaping the country’s future. He stated that India aspired to become a strong and capable nation so that no one could dictate terms to it, and underscored the importance of national strength in safeguarding the country’s independence, dignity and interests.
Reminding the students that the true height of an individual was measured by the depth of knowledge, strength of character and breadth of compassion, the Vice-President called upon them to always uphold “Nation First – Rashtra Pratham” in their thoughts and actions and to say “No to Drugs.”
Calling upon the University fraternity to renew its commitment to the ideals represented by the Iconic Tower, the Vice-President said that knowledge should be the foundation, wisdom the guiding light, innovation the instrument, compassion the strength and service the ultimate purpose. He expressed the hope that the Tower would stand for generations as a beacon of learning, a monument to aspiration and a celebration of Odisha’s timeless spirit, inspiring generations of students to contribute to the making of a confident, prosperous, compassionate and developed India.
The Vice-President also visited the state-of-the-art planetarium at the newly inaugurated Iconic Tower of Sri Sri University, celebrating the spirit of scientific curiosity, discovery and innovation.

title: Vice-President addresses Orientation Programme for Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly in Bhubaneswar
subtitle:
Vice-President urges legislators to uphold democratic values and strengthen public trust through dedicated service

Healthy debate, constructive cooperation essential for strengthening democracy: Vice-President

Vice-President calls for greater use of AI and digital technologies in legislative functioning

Odisha’s progress will be central to India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 NOV 2026 12:39PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today addressed the Orientation Programme for the Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly in Bhubaneswar. Calling upon legislators to uphold the rich democratic traditions of Bharat, he emphasised the importance of constructive debates, informed discussions, legislative efficiency and people-centric governance in strengthening democratic institutions.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the Orientation Programme for the Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly in Bhubaneswar today.

He emphasised the importance of constructive debates, informed discussions, adherence to legislative procedures and embracing emerging technologies to strengthen democratic institutions. He urged legislators to uphold Bharat’s rich democratic traditions and work towards a developed Odisha, contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

Governor of Odisha, Shri Braj Mohan Ram; Chief Minister, Shri Mohan Charan Majhi; Speaker of the Odisha Legislative Assembly, Smt. Surama Padhy;along with Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly were present on the occasion.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
November 16, 2026
The Vice-President appreciated the Speaker, Smt. Surama Padhy, for organising the orientation programme, describing such initiatives as instrumental in strengthening democratic institutions and enabling legislators to discharge their constitutional responsibilities effectively.
Referring to India’s ancient democratic traditions, the Vice-President cited the democratic institutions of Vaishali and the Chola-era Kudavolai system, observing that democracy has deep roots in Bharat’s civilisational history. He said that Bharat rightly takes pride in being the ‘Mother of Democracy’ and called upon the legislators of Odisha to live up to this distinguished legacy.
Emphasising that electoral victories must translate into meaningful public service, the Vice-President said, “We win in the elections by votes, but we can earn the respect of the people only through our service." He observed that the Legislative Assembly is much more than a forum for debate, as every policy framed, question raised and law enacted has the potential to improve the lives of countless citizens.
Referring to the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he said that Odisha’s progress would be central to India’s progress. With Odisha approaching the centenary of its formation as a province in 2036, he highlighted the significance of Vision Odisha 2036 in transforming the State into a developed, prosperous and inclusive State. He expressed confidence that legislators would play an important role in creating opportunities for the youth and ensuring that development reaches every village and every family.
Addressing the issue of disruptions in legislative proceedings, the Vice-President emphasised that differences of opinion should not come in the way of the larger commitment to the people and the Constitution. He remarked, “In a democracy, we may agree to disagree, but we should all agree towards one thing – our commitment to the people and the Constitution.” Reiterating that “debate, discussion or even sometimes disruption must lead to a decision”, he called for healthy debates and constructive cooperation to strengthen democracy and advance national development.
Underscoring the importance of continuous learning and preparation, the Vice-President urged Members to familiarise themselves thoroughly with legislative rules and procedures, budgetary processes, committee systems, parliamentary conventions and ethics.
He particularly highlighted the importance of Question Hour and Zero Hour, describing them as crucial opportunities for individual Members to raise constituency-related concerns and important policy matters. He urged Members to cooperate with the Chair to ensure that these important parliamentary instruments function without disruption.
The Vice-President also emphasised the role of the Business Advisory Committee (BAC) in building consensus on the business of the House. He observed that greater agreement within the Committee would contribute to smoother and more productive legislative proceedings.
Highlighting the growing role of technology in legislative functioning, the Vice-President welcomed the inauguration of the Digital House in the Odisha Legislative Assembly under the National e-Vidhan Application. Referring to the increasing use of digital platforms in the Rajya Sabha, he noted that parliamentary papers, questions and debates were now available in multiple languages with the support of technology. He urged legislators to embrace emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence and Natural Language Processing, to make legislative institutions future-ready.
Concluding his address, the Vice-President reminded legislators of the immense responsibility and transformative potential of their office. He observed that a thoughtful intervention could bring about a change in policy, while a compassionate decision could restore hope in the lives of countless citizens. He wished all Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly a fruitful orientation programme and an enriching legislative journey.
The programme was attended by Governor of Odisha, Shri Braj Mohan Ram; Chief Minister of Odisha, Shri Mohan Charan Majhi; Speaker of the Odisha Legislative Assembly,Smt. Surama Padhy; Deputy Speaker of Odisha Legislative Assembly Shri Bhabani Shankar Bhoi; and Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly, among other dignitaries.

content:
India is hosting the 62nd Session and Ministerial Meeting of the International Coconut Community (ICC) from 17 to 20 November 2026 a
t
Kochi, Kerala. The international event is being jointly organised by the Coconut Development Board (CDB), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India, and the International Coconut Community (ICC), Jakarta, Indonesia.
Established in 1969 under the aegis of the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UN-ESCAP), the International Coconut Community is an inter-governmental organisation comprising of  coconut-producing countries. It provides a common platform for member countries to deliberate on issues concerning the development of the global coconut sector, promote cooperation and partnerships, and explore opportunities for the sustainable growth of the coconut industry.
The 62nd Session is expected to witness the participation of  Shri Ram Nath Thakur, Union Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India, along with Ministers and senior government representatives from ICC member countries across the Asia-Pacific region. Representatives of international organisations, scientists, researchers, industry stakeholders and other distinguished delegates who  are also expected to participate in the meeting.
The inaugural programme will be held on 17 November 2026 at  Kochi will be inaugurated by Shri Ram Nath Thakur, Union Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India. Shri Atish Chandra, IAS, Secretary (Agriculture), Government of India, will deliver the Presidential Address.
Special remarks will be delivered by Hon. Anthony Muller, Minister of Natural Resources and Commerce, Marshall Islands; Hon. Tangriki Reete, Associate Minister of Tourism, Commerce, Industry and Cooperatives, Kiribati; and Hon. H.E. Aiolupotea Misa Tony Aiolupo, Associate Minister of Agriculture and Fisheries, Samoa.
As part of the inaugural ceremony, ICC Plaques of Appreciation will be presented in recognition of excellence in the coconut sector under three categories: Best National Coconut Farmer, Outstanding Coconut Scientist/Researcher and Best National Coconut Entrepreneur.
The four-day Session and Ministerial Meeting will provide an important opportunity for member countries to deliberate on key issues relating to the global coconut industry, share experiences and best practices, strengthen international cooperation and explore collaborative approaches to address emerging challenges and opportunities in the sector. The meeting is expected to facilitate greater cooperation among coconut-producing countries and strengthen collective efforts towards the sustainable development of the global coconut industry.

title: India and Thailand Review Bilateral Trade and Economic Cooperation at 14th Joint Trade Committee Meeting in Nonthaburi, Thailand
subtitle:
India-Thailand Bilateral Trade Grows 12.6% to USD 21.49 Billion in FY 2025-26

India and Thailand Discuss UPI Linkage, Local Currency Settlement and FinTech Cooperation
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 NOV 2026 7:34PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 14th Meeting of the India-Thailand Joint Trade Committee (JTC) was held on 16 November 2026 at the Ministry of Commerce, Nonthaburi, Thailand. The meeting was co-chaired by Additional Secretary, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Shri Nitin Kumar Yadav, and Director-General, Department of Trade Negotiations, Ministry of Commerce, Thailand, Ms. Chotima Iemsawasdikul. Representatives of concerned Ministries, Departments and organisations of both countries also participated.
Both sides noted the encouraging momentum in bilateral trade, which reached USD 21.49 billion in FY 2025–26, registering a growth of 12.6 per cent over the previous year. Thailand accounted for 16.7 per cent of India's total trade with ASEAN. The co-chairs acknowledged the role of the JTC in facilitating trade and investment, and reiterated their commitment to expanding bilateral trade and investment and facilitating market access.
India highlighted investment opportunities in infrastructure and logistics, automotive and electric vehicles, food processing and agro-industry, electronics and semiconductors, and tourism, hospitality and wellness. Thailand shared its economic outlook and investment facilitation measures and presented its “Co-Creation Co-Investment” approach. India welcomed the approach and agreed to examine it further in consultation with the concerned Ministries and Departments.
The meeting discussed enhancing the utilisation of the ASEAN–India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) and the India–Thailand Early Harvest Scheme. Both sides also explored a mechanism for the annual exchange of bilateral trade data and data on the utilisation of preferences to identify areas for enhancing preferential trade and addressing implementation-related challenges. They underlined the importance of an early and meaningful conclusion of the AITIGA Review.
The discussions focused on ensuring effective market access and resolving issues faced by traders, including market access for agricultural, livestock and marine products, sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) measures and certification processes, quality and regulatory requirements, and the removal of non-tariff barriers.
Both sides explored opportunities for cooperation in pharmaceuticals and healthcare, AYUSH and traditional medicine, textiles, plastics and petrochemicals, gems and jewellery, as well as the services sector. Collaboration between trade promotion organisations was also discussed.
The two sides also deliberated on payment and financial connectivity, including the linkage of India's UPI with Thailand's PromptPay, local currency settlement and FinTech cooperation between the Reserve Bank of India and the Bank of Thailand.
The meeting reaffirmed the commitment of both sides to strengthening the India–Thailand economic partnership. The co-chairs encouraged officials to continue discussions and convene working-level meetings before the next JTC meeting to sustain the momentum. The next meeting of the JTC will be held in India.

title: 12th Session of India–Belarus Inter-Governmental Commission held in New Delhi
subtitle:
Minister of State Shri Jitin Prasada and Belarusian Foreign Minister Mr. Maxim Ryzhenkov co-chair the Session

Both sides review bilateral cooperation and discuss measures to strengthen trade, economic and investment relations

India–Belarus Business and Investment Forum held alongside the Session to explore opportunities for greater business engagement
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 NOV 2026 6:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 12th Session of the India–Belarus Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation was held on 16th November 2026 in New Delhi. Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Shri Jitin Prasada led the Indian delegation, while Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Belarus H.E. Mr. Maxim Ryzhenkov led the Belarusian delegation.
The Session reviewed the progress of bilateral cooperation and discussed measures to further strengthen trade, economic and investment relations between the two countries. Both sides appreciated the longstanding and friendly relations between India and Belarus and highlighted the importance of regular exchanges, closer institutional engagement and greater participation of businesses in taking the partnership forward.
Discussions covered several important areas of economic cooperation, with a focus on expanding bilateral trade and investment. Both sides also discussed the Roadmap for Cooperation for 2027–2031 as an important step towards identifying future priorities and providing direction to bilateral economic engagement. Key sectors discussed included industry, financial and banking services, agriculture and food processing, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, tourism, education, culture, science and technology, construction and customs cooperation.
The Protocol of the 12th Session of the India–Belarus Inter-Governmental Commission was signed by both Co-Chairs, reaffirming the commitment of the two countries to deepen bilateral cooperation.
Addressing the business community, Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Shri Jitin Prasada highlighted India's growing economic and manufacturing capabilities and the opportunities they offer for closer engagement with Belarusian businesses. He emphasised that the longstanding friendship between the two countries provides a strong foundation for building practical and mutually beneficial economic partnerships. He also encouraged businesses to explore joint ventures, technology partnerships, investment opportunities and greater business-to-business engagement.
Shri Jitin Prasada highlighted the potential for collaboration in areas such as pharmaceuticals, agricultural and industrial machinery, engineering, chemicals, digital technologies and scientific research. He also encouraged businesses from both countries to explore opportunities for market access, local partnerships, co-development and cooperation in emerging areas, including unmanned aerial systems and advanced manufacturing technologies.
On the sidelines of the 12th Session of the Inter-Governmental Commission, the India–Belarus Business and Investment Forum was also organised in New Delhi on 16th November 2026. The Forum brought together business representatives, industry associations and government institutions from India and Belarus, providing an opportunity for direct interaction, exchange of ideas and exploration of new areas of trade, investment and commercial cooperation.
The Forum saw participation from Belarusian companies representing diverse sectors, including automotive and agricultural machinery, mining equipment, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, microelectronics, banking, agriculture and engineering. Discussions focused on possibilities for joint ventures, technology transfer, localisation of manufacturing, research and development, and stronger supply-chain linkages. Opportunities in agricultural and civil unmanned aerial systems, pharmaceutical cooperation, mining equipment, water treatment technologies and food processing were also highlighted as potential areas for future collaboration.
Both sides underlined the importance of maintaining regular engagement between their business communities and encouraged enterprises to take forward the opportunities identified during the discussions.
India and Belarus agreed to continue working together to expand cooperation across the identified sectors and strengthen their economic partnership. Both sides also agreed to hold the 13th Session of the India–Belarus Inter-Governmental Commission in 2027, with the dates and agenda to be finalised through diplomatic channels.

Key highlights of WPI (Base Year 2022-23) for October 2026
All India Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation for October 2026 is 12.29 per cent on year-on-year (YoY) basis, compared to 11.39 per cent in September 2026. The index for All Commodities for October 2026 stands at 113.3, whereas it was 112.5 in September 2026.
YoY inflation rates for major groups, namely, Primary Articles, Fuel and Power, and Manufactured Products are 9.24 per cent, 32.84 per cent, and 9.54 per cent, respectively in October 2026, compared to 8.67 per cent, 25.85 per cent, and 9.76 per cent, respectively in September 2026. The indices for Primary Articles, Fuel and Power, and Manufactured Products are 120.6, 115.7, and 110.2, respectively, in October 2026, whereas they were 120.3, 110.5, and 110.2, respectively, in September 2026.
Across groups, ‘Mineral Oils
(containing Petroleum Products)
’, ‘Crude Petroleum and Natural Gas’, ‘Electricity’, ‘Food Articles’, ‘Manufacture of Basic Metals’, ‘Manufacture of Chemicals and Chemical Products’, ‘Manufacture of Food Products’, ‘Non-Food Articles’, ‘Manufacture of Textiles’, and ‘Manufacture of Rubber and Plastic Products’ have been drivers of WPI inflation in October 2026.
WPI Food Index (weight=24.99 per cent):
The Food Index consists of ‘Food Articles’ from Primary Articles major group, and ‘Manufacture of Food Products’ from Manufactured Products major group. It observed a YoY inflation of 8.58 per cent in October 2026, compared to 8.66 per cent in September 2026.

The final index for the month of August 2026 remains unchanged at 110.8 as compared to the provisional index. Accordingly, the WPI inflation rate for August 2026 also remains unchanged at 9.92 per cent (final).
The final index of WPI (Base Year 2022-23) for the month of August 2026 has been compiled with a weighted response rate of 99.37 per cent.
The provisional index of WPI (Base Year 2022-23) for the month of October 2026 has been compiled with a weighted response rate of 81.1 per cent.

title: NICDC Showcases Andhra Pradesh's Industrial Progress and Investment Opportunities at 31st CII Partnership Summit 2026 in Visakhapatnam
subtitle:
CEO & MD, NICDC, Briefs Dignitaries on Progress of Three Industrial Nodes in Andhra Pradesh

Summit Focuses on Strengthening Global Partnerships, Attracting Investments and Positioning India as a Global Manufacturing Hub

NICDC Pavilion Showcases Andhra Pradesh’s Industrial Potential, Investment Opportunities and Greenfield Industrial Smart Cities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 NOV 2026 11:33AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) organised the 31st edition of the CII Partnership Summit 2026 on 12–13 November 2026 in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, under the theme “Navigating the New World Order: Trade | Technology | Trust | Thought Leadership.” Organised in association with the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, and hosted by the Government of Andhra Pradesh, the Summit brought together policymakers, international delegates, global business leaders and investors to deliberate on emerging opportunities in trade, technology and economic cooperation.
The inaugural session was attended by Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal; Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh Shri N. Chandrababu Naidu; Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh Shri Konidala Pawan Kalyan; and Union Minister of Civil Aviation Shri Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu. Shri Nara Lokesh, Minister for Human Resources Development, IT, Electronics & Communication and RTG, Government of Andhra Pradesh, also delivered a special address.
The inaugural session also witnessed the participation of several senior leaders, Union and State Ministers, overseas trade ministers, senior government officials, policymakers and prominent industry representatives from India and abroad, reflecting the strong participation in efforts to strengthen international trade, investment, industrial cooperation and strategic partnerships.
The Summit provided a platform for deliberations on international trade, global value chains, resilient supply chains, advanced manufacturing, defence technology, critical minerals, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, smart manufacturing, green energy, future mobility and emerging technologies. Discussions focused on strengthening international partnerships, attracting investments and positioning India as a competitive destination for global manufacturing and innovation.
During the Summit, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh Shri N. Chandrababu Naidu visited the National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC) pavilion. Shri Rajat Kumar Saini, CEO & MD, NICDC, briefed the dignitaries on the development and progress of NICDC's three Greenfield Industrial Smart City nodes in Andhra Pradesh: Krishnapatnam, Orvakal and Kopparthy.
The NICDC pavilion showcased India's evolving industrial infrastructure landscape and investment opportunities through various initiatives and digital platforms. Key highlights included the development of Greenfield Industrial Smart Cities, BHAVYA (Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana), the Industrial Corridor Land Platform (ICLP), which enables investors to discover and compare verified industrial land opportunities across India, and Koyla Shakti, a Smart Coal Analytics Dashboard. The pavilion also featured a 360-degree Virtual Reality (VR) Tour, offering visitors an immersive overview of NICDC's industrial corridor projects.
Shri Rajat Kumar Saini apprised the dignitaries of the development progress of the three industrial nodes. The updates highlighted the progress of infrastructure development across the projects and NICDC's continued efforts towards creating investment-ready industrial destinations in the State.
The pavilion also showcased Andhra Pradesh's industrial potential, highlighting the three nodes' combined project area of 7,223 acres, investment potential of ₹31,360 crore and employment potential of 2 lakh. The three nodes are being developed under different industrial corridors and are envisaged as integrated industrial ecosystems supported by world-class infrastructure and connectivity. Their development is aimed at facilitating large-scale investments, strengthening manufacturing capabilities, generating employment and accelerating industrial growth in Andhra Pradesh.
Through these displays and interactions, NICDC highlighted investment opportunities across manufacturing and emerging sectors, positioning Andhra Pradesh as an attractive destination for domestic and international investors.
During the Japan Country Session, H.E. Mr Keiichi Ono, Ambassador of Japan to India, highlighted the growing India–Japan economic partnership, noting that 31 Japanese companies across three cities in Andhra Pradesh have generated over 8,000 local jobs. He also highlighted opportunities for collaboration in steel, pharmaceuticals, clean energy and semiconductors.
Shri T. G. Bharath, Minister for Industries & Commerce and Food Processing, Government of Andhra Pradesh, highlighted the State's industrial infrastructure, strategic ports, sectoral opportunities and focus on translating investment commitments into project implementation.
Shri Rajat Kumar Saini delivered the opening remarks, outlining five key areas for deeper cooperation: manufacturing and industrial corridor development, resilient supply chains, advanced technologies, sustainable industrial development, and MSME partnerships and skill development. He emphasised the need to translate investment opportunities into actionable partnerships, highlighting Japan's commitment to facilitate investments of JPY 10 trillion in India over the next decade.
Mr Kiyotaka Doho, Director General, JETRO Chennai, highlighted the growing interest among Japanese companies in India and Andhra Pradesh, with over 80 per cent of surveyed companies planning to expand their operations. Mr Rajesh Mittal, President & MD, Isuzu Motors India, underscored the importance of Japanese manufacturing practices, quality standards, skill development and local supplier ecosystems.
Through the development of Greenfield Industrial Smart Cities across various industrial corridors, NICDC is working towards strengthening India's manufacturing ecosystem, enhancing logistics efficiency and creating investment-ready industrial destinations. Its initiatives aim to attract domestic and international investments, generate employment and facilitate the integration of Indian industries with global value chains.
Other distinguished dignitaries present at the event included Shri T. G. Bharath, Minister for Industries and Food Processing, Government of Andhra Pradesh; Shri B. C. Janardhan Reddy, Minister for Roads and Buildings, Infrastructure and Investments, Government of Andhra Pradesh; Shri G. Sai Prasad, Chief Secretary to the Government of Andhra Pradesh; Shri R. Mukundan, President, CII and Managing Director & CEO, Tata Chemicals Limited; and Shri Chandrajit Banerjee, Director General, CII.
NICDC's participation in the 31st CII Partnership Summit 2026 provided an opportunity to showcase the progress of its industrial corridor projects, engage with global stakeholders and highlight investment opportunities in Andhra Pradesh. These efforts contribute to the Government of India's vision of strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities and achieving Viksit Bharat @2047.
National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation Limited (NICDC), under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, is mandated to develop world-class Greenfield Industrial Smart Cities across the country. Through integrated industrial infrastructure and digital initiatives, NICDC aims to enhance manufacturing competitiveness, attract investments and promote sustainable economic development.

title: India and Egypt Hold Ministerial-Level 7th Joint Trade Committee Meeting to Strengthen Bilateral Economic Ties
subtitle:
Both sides agree to set up a Joint Working Group to explore Terms of Reference for a Preferential or Free Trade Agreement

India–Egypt bilateral trade grows 35% to USD 6.5 billion in FY 2025-26; trade during April–September 2026 rises 65% to USD 5.04 billion

More than 300 Indian and Egyptian companies participate in India–Egypt Business Forum to explore trade, investment and manufacturing partnerships
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 NOV 2026 9:37AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and H.E. Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt, co-chaired the 7th session of the India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC) in Egypt’s New Administrative Capital today. The meeting marked the first occasion on which this important bilateral institutional mechanism was convened at the ministerial level, underscoring the priority both governments attach to strengthening the economic dimension of the India–Egypt Strategic Partnership.
Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to expanding bilateral trade, with a target of USD 12 billion. They emphasised the need to diversify trade, promote value-added exports and address trade-related challenges. As a key outcome of the 7th Joint Trade Committee meeting, both Ministers agreed to establish a Joint Working Group to explore the Terms of Reference for a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement to facilitate stronger bilateral trade, improve access to both markets and promote investment linkages between the two countries.
The meeting was preceded by bilateral discussions between the two Ministers on expanding trade, facilitating investments and developing long-term industrial and commercial linkages. The JTC provided an opportunity to review existing trade ties, assess challenges faced by businesses and identify new areas for closer collaboration.
The Committee reviewed the growth in India–Egypt trade, which increased by 35% to reach USD 6.5 billion in FY 2025-26 (April 2025–March 2026). Trade during April–September 2026 also grew by 65% to reach USD 5.04 billion, compared to USD 3.08 billion during the corresponding period in 2025. The increase reflects the growing momentum in commercial exchanges and the potential for further diversification of the trade basket. Significant complementarities exist for enhanced trade in industrial goods, energy and fertilisers, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, engineering, textiles and agricultural products.
The discussions primarily focused on expanding trade, developing supply chains and establishing predictable trade pathways. Both sides considered measures to address non-tariff barriers, facilitate customs processes, strengthen standards and conformity assessment, and improve market access. They also discussed practical issues affecting business operations, including product registrations and trade-related regulatory procedures.
Discussions also focused on strengthening business exchanges and encouraging joint manufacturing and investment. Priority sectors included pharmaceuticals and medical devices, engineering and electrical equipment, fertilisers, textiles, renewable energy and emerging technologies. Opportunities for Indian investment in Egyptian industrial zones, as well as Egyptian investment in India's expanding manufacturing and services sectors, also formed an important part of the agenda.
Both sides expressed interest in strengthening the framework agreement between Invest India and Egypt’s General Authority for Investment and Free Zones, including a proposed digital platform for sharing investment information and facilitating business linkages.
Egypt’s proximity to the Suez Canal and its connectivity with African, Arab and European markets make it a valuable partner for export-oriented manufacturing and regional supply chains. India, in turn, offers Egyptian investors and exporters a large and dynamic market, increasingly competitive infrastructure and opportunities for technology and production partnerships.
Speaking at the Joint Trade Committee meeting, Shri Piyush Goyal highlighted five areas of strong complementarity between India and Egypt: pharmaceuticals and healthcare, leveraging India’s strengths in affordable medicines, vaccines and medical technology; engineering and automobiles, covering machinery, auto components and industrial manufacturing; agriculture and food processing, including food security, fertilisers, irrigation and cold-chain infrastructure; digital and fintech, through UPI linkages, local currency trade and India’s Digital Public Infrastructure; and culture and museums, through proposed collaboration between the Grand Egyptian Museum and India’s upcoming Yuge Yugeen Bharat National Museum in conservation, curation and digitisation.
The ministerial-level JTC is an important step towards advancing the economic priorities of the India–Egypt Strategic Partnership. It was held against the backdrop of the meeting between President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi during the BRICS Summit in India in September 2026. The JTC seeks to translate this political momentum into stronger trade flows, new investments, joint manufacturing, greater market access and more resilient supply chains connecting India, Egypt and wider regional markets.
The next JTC meeting was agreed to be held in New Delhi in 2028, or earlier at a mutually convenient date.
The India–Egypt Business Forum brought together more than 300 companies from India and Egypt today, providing a platform to strengthen business engagement under the India–Egypt Strategic Partnership. Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and H.E. Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt, addressed the Forum, which was attended by industry leaders and senior business representatives from a wide range of sectors.
The Forum was organised on the sidelines of Shri Piyush Goyal’s official visit to Egypt from 15 to 16 November 2026. The opening session was addressed by Dr. Mohamed Awad, Chief Executive Officer of the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI); Mr. Vijay Sankar, President of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) and Chairman of Sanmar Group; and Mr. Ahmed ElWakil, President of the Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce.
Addressing the session, Shri Goyal proposed a four-point action agenda ahead of the 80th anniversary of India–Egypt diplomatic relations in 2027. The agenda included resolving identified trade barriers within a time-bound framework; encouraging Egyptian investments in Indian states and industrial clusters, with Invest India facilitating opportunities; bringing suppliers of large companies into the partnership to create opportunities for smaller businesses; and institutionalising annual reviews to track progress and translate business discussions into concrete contracts.
Underscoring the ambition of the partnership, Shri Goyal said, "Years from now, when someone studies this decade, let them find factories with labels that say: Made in Egypt, with India. Made in India, with Egypt."
A dedicated session on investment opportunities in Egypt brought together senior representatives of GAFI and the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE), who presented the country’s industrial and investment opportunities. Egypt’s strategic location linking the Mediterranean and Red Seas, its expanding ports and logistics infrastructure, and its access to African, Arab and European markets offer opportunities for Indian businesses seeking to establish manufacturing and export-oriented operations.
The Forum also featured a session on the experiences of Indian companies operating in Egypt, including TCI Sanmar, Galaxy Chemical and Abdos. Their presence illustrated the potential for Indian investments to contribute to Egyptian industrial production, employment, technology development, exports and integration into regional supply chains. Representatives of the two business communities explored areas of cooperation in engineering and electrical equipment, chemicals and fertilisers, pharmaceuticals, textiles, food processing, automotive components, renewable energy and logistics.
A special panel on the digital economy brought together stakeholders from Egypt’s digital technology and transformation ecosystem and leading Indian startups and technology companies. Moderated by Eng. Ayman El Gohary, Chairman of Global for Smart Solutions, the panel included experts and industry leaders from both countries. The Egyptian participants included Eng. Mahmoud Sofrata of the Information Technology Industry Development Agency (ITIDA), Mr. Fady Ismaeel of AGX, Dr. Kareem Hamza of National System and Dr. Sideek Ahmed of Eram Holding. Indian industry representatives included Mr. Rajesh Ranganathan of Zoho and Mr. Pradeep Gilbile of Datamorphosis. The discussions focused on opportunities in enterprise technology, digital solutions, innovation and industry partnerships.
Earlier in the day, the 6th India–Egypt Joint Business Council (JBC) meeting was held at the New Administrative Capital. Shri Goyal and Minister Saleh addressed the Council. The Council was co-chaired by Mr. Ganesh Kumar, Executive Vice Chairman, TCI Sanmar Chemicals SAE, on the Indian side, and Mr. Khaled Aboul Makarem of Makarem Tex on the Egyptian side. Mr. Vijay Sankar, President of FICCI, also addressed the Council.
The Joint Business Council provided a platform for focused discussions on priority sectors, including chemicals and petrochemicals, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, food processing and agri-business, renewable energy and green hydrogen, infrastructure, ports and logistics, information technology and digital services, textiles and automotive manufacturing. The Council also examined ways to strengthen institutional links between business organisations, including the possibility of establishing sectoral working groups, customs and trade facilitation, business visas and a calendar of reciprocal trade missions for 2026-27.
The two engagements highlighted the complementarities between the Indian and Egyptian economies. India offers a large and growing market, competitive manufacturing, engineering and digital capabilities, while Egypt offers an established industrial base, strategic connectivity, skilled human resources and access to markets in Africa and the wider region. Bilateral trade exceeds USD 6.5 billion, while Indian investments in Egypt already exceed USD 5.5 billion. Both sides see significant potential for deeper two-way investment, joint manufacturing, technology partnerships and the development of supply chains serving domestic and international markets.
Shri Goyal’s visit follows the meeting between President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi during the September 2026 BRICS Summit in India. The high-level visit, the India–Egypt Business Forum involving more than 300 companies and the India–Egypt Joint Business Council engagements reflect the shared ambition to further strengthen economic engagement under the India–Egypt Strategic Partnership.
Shri Piyush Goyal held a bilateral meeting with H.E. Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt, to review bilateral trade and investment relations and explore avenues for further economic cooperation. Discussions covered trade expansion, market access, investment opportunities, pharmaceuticals, fertilisers and challenges faced by Indian businesses in Egypt, including visa-related issues. Shri Goyal emphasised the importance of facilitating Indian investments and strengthening bilateral supply chains and business-to-business linkages.Shri Piyush Goyal also held a bilateral meeting with H.E. Eng. Khaled Hashem, Minister of Industry of Egypt, to discuss opportunities for strengthening industrial cooperation, promoting manufacturing partnerships and enhancing investment linkages. Both sides discussed potential cooperation in industrial development, technology partnerships, MSME development, industrial automation and advanced manufacturing.

title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah visits the Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) in Pune and reviews its functioning and progress of various initiatives
subtitle:
Shri Amit Shah interacts with officials and reviews activities related to registration, regulation, monitoring and good governance of Multi-State Cooperative Societies

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation emphasises transparent, accountable and systematic development of cooperative societies in Maharashtra and the Western Region in accordance with the National Cooperation Policy

Shri Amit Shah stresses the need for effective monitoring of cooperative societies and strict compliance with regulatory provisions to prevent potential irregularities

CRCS Regional Office in Pune oversees matters relating to 818 Multi-State Cooperative Societies registered across Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

Of the 1,872 Multi-State Cooperative Societies registered across the country, 420 have been registered since the formation of the Ministry of Cooperation

Regional Offices in Pune, Lucknow, Chennai and Kolkata will strengthen monitoring, grievance redressal and regulatory functions relating to Multi-State Cooperative Societies
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 NOV 2026 9:59PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of
'Sahkar se Samriddhi'
, transparency, accountability, good governance and institutional strengthening in the cooperative sector are being continuously promoted under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah. As part of these efforts, Shri Amit Shah today visited the Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) in Pune, Maharashtra. During the visit, he interacted with officials and reviewed the progress of various initiatives relating to the registration, regulation, monitoring and reform of Multi-State Cooperative Societies. Shri Amit Shah particularly sought information regarding the functioning of cooperative societies in Maharashtra, their registration status and measures being taken to further strengthen the regulatory framework. The establishment of Regional Offices of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies is a significant initiative towards ensuring effective regulation of Multi-State Cooperative Societies and decentralisation of cooperative administration across the country.
During the review, Shri Amit Shah emphasised that the development of Multi-State Cooperative Societies in Maharashtra and the Western Region must be aligned with the objectives and guidelines of the National Cooperation Policy. He stated that the role of the Regional Office should not remain confined merely to registration-related activities but should extend to ensuring effective supervision, regulatory compliance, transparency and accountability in the functioning of cooperative societies.
The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation also reviewed ongoing activities with the officials and emphasised that registration, inspection, auditing, grievance redressal and other statutory processes relating to cooperative societies must be carried out in a transparent and time-bound manner. He underscored the importance of an effective regulatory framework to promote good governance in cooperative institutions and safeguard the interests of all stakeholders, including members and depositors.
The Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) is a statutory authority under the Ministry of Cooperation, appointed under Article 243ZH(f) of the Constitution and Section 4(1) of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002. It regulates cooperative societies whose objectives and areas of operation extend beyond the boundaries of a single State. The CRCS is entrusted with important statutory powers and responsibilities, including registration and regulation of Multi-State Cooperative Societies, amendments to their registered bye-laws, supersession of Boards in accordance with statutory provisions, inquiries, inspections, audits, settlement of disputes, and liquidation and winding up of defunct societies.
At present, a total of 1,872 Multi-State Cooperative Societies are registered across the country. Of these, 420 societies have been registered since the establishment of the Ministry of Cooperation on 6 July 2021. In view of the increasing number of Multi-State Cooperative Societies and their expanding geographical presence, Regional Offices are being established to ensure effective monitoring, regulatory compliance and good governance.
The first Regional Office of the CRCS, established in Pune for the Western Region, oversees matters relating to 818 Multi-State Cooperative Societies registered across Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. These include 756 societies in Maharashtra, 59 in Gujarat, two in Goa and one in Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. Thus, a substantial proportion of the country's registered Multi-State Cooperative Societies falls within the jurisdiction of the Pune Regional Office.
The Pune Regional Office commenced its operations on 15 April 2026. The Department of Expenditure has sanctioned 10 posts for the office. Arrangements are being made for the deployment of officers and essential support personnel to ensure effective and timely execution of regulatory functions relating to Multi-State Cooperative Societies.
To further strengthen the monitoring and administrative framework for Multi-State Cooperative Societies, the Ministry of Cooperation has initiated steps to establish additional Regional Offices in Lucknow for the Northern Region, Chennai for the Southern Region and Kolkata for the Eastern and North-Eastern Regions, in addition to the Pune office. These offices will facilitate decentralisation of regulatory administration, faster approval processes, improved monitoring and compliance, greater financial inclusion, effective grievance redressal and expansion of digital services.
The Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies has also undertaken several important initiatives for the digitisation, reform and strengthening of Multi-State Cooperative Societies. These include the development of an online system for processes such as registration of societies, amendments to bye-laws, filing of annual returns and opening of branches. Other significant measures include amendments to the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, computerisation of the offices of the Cooperative Election Authority and the Cooperative Ombudsman, and the establishment of the Cooperative Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Development Fund (CRRDF).
In a significant step towards strengthening financial discipline, transparency and accountability in Multi-State Cooperative Societies, the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Auditor's Report) Order, 2026 (MSCARO, 2026) has also been issued. These reforms aim to ensure better financial management, effective regulatory oversight and protection of the interests of members of cooperative institutions.
The visit of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah to the Pune Regional Office marks an important step towards strengthening the regulation of Multi-State Cooperative Societies, enhancing the effectiveness of regional monitoring mechanisms and promoting transparency, accountability and good governance in the cooperative sector in accordance with the National Cooperation Policy.

title: CCPA Imposes Penalty of ₹20 Lakh on ExportersIndia.com (Weblink.In Pvt. Ltd.) in Two Orders for Online Listing of Ammonium Nitrate, PETN and Picric Acid
subtitle: Penalties and Directions Upheld; Appeals Dismissed by NCDRC
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 NOV 2026 4:50PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC), New Delhi, through two orders dated
12 November 2026
, has dismissed the appeals filed by
Weblink.In Private Limited
, operator of ExportersIndia.com, against two final orders of the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA). The NCDRC has thereby upheld in full the
penalties and directions issued by the CCPA
for the online listing, hosting, advertising and facilitation of sale of regulated and hazardous explosive substances on the platform.
following the CCPA's earlier sector-wide action against such listings on e-commerce platforms
.
Background: CCPA's Action Against Online Listing of Explosive Substances
The CCPA, headed by
Chief Commissioner Smt. Nidhi Khare and Commissioner Shri Anupam Mishra
, in exercise of its powers under Sections 18 and 19 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, carried out a sector-wide review of e-commerce platforms to examine whether hazardous chemicals, explosive substances and related precursors, namely
Ammonium Nitrate, Gun Powder, Picric Acid and Pentaerythritol Tetranitrate (PETN)
, were being listed, hosted, advertised or made available for sale online.
These substances are regulated, restricted or prohibited under the
Explosives Act, 1884
and the rules framed under it. Picric Acid stands declared an explosive by Notification GSR 625(E) dated 7 August 1983, while Ammonium Nitrate is regulated under the
Ammonium Nitrate Rules, 2012
.
The CCPA found that several platforms were enabling access to these highly sensitive materials without disclosure of the seller's valid
PESO (Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation) licence
, verification of the identity and licensed status of the buyer, traceability safeguards or caution regarding the legal restrictions on their possession and use.
The platforms examined included
IndiaMART, Justdial, Dial4Trade, Sigma-Aldrich India, ExportersIndia, Ibuychemikals and TradeIndia
. Following the CCPA's intervention, the listings of these substances were delisted from the platforms.
Two CCPA Final Orders Against Weblink.In Private Limited
After issuing Show Cause Notices to the company, calling for an investigation by the Director General (Investigation), sharing the investigation reports with the company, considering its written replies and hearing its counsel, the CCPA passed two separate final orders under Sections 20 and 21 read with Section 10 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019:
Final Order dated 08.09.2026:
Relating to the listing of Ammonium Nitrate and PETN.
Final Order dated 10.09.2026:
Relating to the listing of Picric Acid.
Both orders were challenged by the company before the NCDRC.
Under each order, the CCPA imposed a penalty of
₹10 lakh
, taking the total penalty to
₹20 lakh
. It also directed the company to
permanently discontinue the listing, hosting, advertising or facilitation of sale of, or enquiry for, such substances
and any other substance classified as an explosive under the Explosives Act, 1884 or the Explosive Substances Act, 1908.
CCPA's Findings: Misleading Advertisements and Unfair Trade Practices
The CCPA held that the conduct amounted to a
misleading advertisement and an unfair trade practice
under Sections 2(28) and 2(47) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and violated the right of consumers under Section 2(9) to be protected against the marketing of goods hazardous to life and property.
The platform displayed Ammonium Nitrate, PETN and Picric Acid like ordinary products, with price quote options and an invitation to "Get Best Quotes". However, it did not disclose that these substances are notified explosives, that a licence is required to buy or sell them, or that unauthorised possession is punishable. It also displayed a "verified" tick against sellers of explosives, although the company admitted that it did not check the licence of any seller or buyer. This gave buyers the false impression that these substances could be freely and lawfully purchased.
The CCPA further observed that the platform earned fees through paid memberships and a paid V-Trust Certificate, but failed to put in place basic safeguards. The key deficiencies identified included:
Non-disclosure of sellers' PESO licences.
Failure to verify the identity and licensed status of buyers.
Absence of traceability safeguards
as required under the Ammonium Nitrate Rules, 2012.
Failure to provide warnings
regarding the legal restrictions on possession and use of these substances.
The company's claim that it was only a B2B directory was not accepted, as anyone could register with just a phone number and e-mail address and post a requirement for any quantity. Since explosives could thereby reach persons with no legal right to hold them, the CCPA held that consumers and the public were exposed to serious risk, in violation of Section 2(9). It also held that the
Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020
applied to the platform.
Safe Harbour Defence Rejected by CCPA and NCDRC
Before both forums, the company argued that it was only an intermediary protected by Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000, that it had no actual knowledge of the listings and that no law required it to verify licences of sellers or buyers of explosives.
The CCPA rejected these pleas. It held that safe harbour under Section 79 is conditional on due diligence under Section 79(2)(c) and Rule 3(1)(b) of the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021. The "actual knowledge" standard laid down in
Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
governs takedown of specific content on notice, but does not remove the independent duty to exercise due diligence at the point of listing. A compliance approach that only removes listings after detection was held to be insufficient for regulated and hazardous substances.
The NCDRC affirmed this position. It held that the platform could not plead selective diligence, that knowledge of the notifications declaring these substances to be explosives could be ascribed to such facilitators and that the company could not claim immunity under Section 79 of the IT Act.
The NCDRC also rejected the argument that no statute required licence verification. It observed that a platform must take reasonable care and exercise due diligence when its space is used to advertise trade in hazardous substances, and that the advertisements carried none of the categorical cautions that such substances demand.
The NCDRC found that the CCPA had acted within its jurisdiction after following the principles of natural justice and that there was
no infirmity, perversity or error of law
in its orders. In the second appeal, it dismissed the challenge for the same reasons.
Action Against Other E-Commerce Platforms
The CCPA has also taken action against other platforms examined during the sector-wide review:
Dial4Trade Technologies Private Limited:
A penalty of ₹10 lakh was imposed for listing Ammonium Nitrate. The NCDRC dismissed its appeal on
09.10.2026
.
Just Dial Limited:
A penalty of
₹10 lakh
has likewise been imposed.
Proceedings against the remaining platforms examined in this exercise, including
India MART InterMESH Limited, Sigma-Aldrich Chemicals Private Limited, TradeIndia (Infocom Network Private Limited) and Ibuychemikals
, remain under investigation.
CCPA Reiterates Commitment to Consumer Protection
The two NCDRC orders reaffirm that platforms which host or promote listings of regulated and hazardous goods must
exercise due diligence before listing such products
and cannot rely on intermediary status to avoid responsibility under consumer protection law.
The CCPA reiterates its commitment to protecting consumers and the public from the unregulated online availability of hazardous substances and ensuring that e-commerce platforms comply with due-diligence requirements.
Any instance of explosives being offered for sale on an online platform may be reported to the
National Consumer Helpline at 1915
.

title: MoD & MoSJE ink MoU to strengthen welfare of senior citizens in Cantonment areas
subtitle:
The MoU envisages establishment & strengthening of Day Care Centres and Senior Citizen Homes along with skill training of geriatric caregivers

Senior citizens, with their experience and wisdom, will make significant contributions towards achieving Viksit Bharat@2047; their welfare is a social & moral responsibility: Raksha Mantri

Govt is committed to ensuring dignified, secure & active ageing for all senior citizens: Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 NOV 2026 1:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Defence, through the Directorate General of Defence Estates (DGDE), has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment (MoSJE) to strengthen the welfare of senior citizens residing in Cantonment areas. Inked in the presence of Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh and Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr Virendra Kumar in New Delhi on November 16, 2026, the MoU envisages the establishment and strengthening of Day Care Centres and Senior Citizen Homes, along with skill training of geriatric caregivers.
In his address, Raksha Mantri described the elderly as not merely family members, but also bearers of experience, traditions and social consciousness, whose experience, wisdom and guidance will be invaluable in the journey towards Viksit Bharat by 2047. Highlighting their lifelong contribution to building families, society and the nation, he termed it a social and moral responsibility to ensure that they are accorded respect, security and a sense of belonging. “Our cultural values teach us ‘Matru Devo Bhava, Pitru Devo Bhava’. Caring for the elderly is not just a family matter; it is our responsibility,” he said.
While acknowledging the progress made in senior citizen welfare, Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised the need for continuous improvement in the delivery of services to the elderly. He called for social audits of the Centres and Homes to assess the quality of services, and identify areas requiring further improvement.
Speaking on the occasion, the Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment reiterated the Government’s commitment to the welfare of senior citizens and enumerated the initiatives taken by MoSJE, including the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), to improve the quality of life of the elderly. He stated that the MoU marks an important step towards strengthening the support system for senior citizens residing in Cantonment areas by ensuring access to better care, welfare services and opportunities for active and dignified ageing.
Dr Virendra Kumar also described senior citizens as bearers of invaluable experience and wisdom, whose knowledge and contributions can play an important role in nation-building. “Our soldiers safeguard the nation’s borders with courage, sacrifice and dedication. It is our collective responsibility to ensure that they receive the care, respect and support they deserve,” he added.
Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary, Department of Social Justice & Empowerment Shri Sudhansh Pant, Director General, Defence Estates Smt Shobha Gupta and other senior officials of the two Ministries were present on the occasion.
About the MoU
Under the proposed arrangement, MoSJE will extend financial assistance under AVYAY, including support towards the operation and maintenance of existing Day Care Centres and Senior Citizen Homes being run by Cantonment Boards from their own budgets. Ambala (Haryana), Deolali (Maharashtra), Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh), Ranikhet & Lansdowne (Uttarakhand) Cantonments already run Day Care Centres and Ayodhya and Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh) Cantonments run senior citizen homes from their own budgets which are primarily dependent on grants from the Ministry of Defence.
The MoU envisages establishing new Day Care Centres/Senior Citizen Homes in Cantonments under AVYAY Scheme. DGDE has identified eight Cantonments where new day care centres can be opened. Existing day care centres in five Cantonments and senior citizen homes in two Cantonments would also be augmented in consultation with MoSJE as per availability of funds. The Cantonments identified for opening of new centres by DGDE are Barrackpore (West Bengal), Belgaum (Karnataka), Jhansi (Uttar Pradesh), Khadki & Pune (Maharashtra), Secunderabad (Telangana), St. Thomas Mount (Tamil Nadu) and Delhi. The existing five cantonments where Day Care Centres are proposed to be strengthened are Ambala (Haryana), Deolali (Maharashtra), Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh), Ranikhet & Lansdowne (Uttarakhand). Senior citizen homes in Ayodhya and Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh) cantonments are also proposed to be augmented.
DGDE and Cantonment Boards will make available suitable premises and essential infrastructure, including electricity, water supply and sanitation, while MoSJE will provide financial assistance, technical guidance, training modules and operational support under the scheme.
Another important component of the MoU is skill training of young Indians in geriatric caregiving. With India’s elderly population steadily increasing, the demand for trained caregivers and specialised elderly care services is expected to grow in the coming years. The initiative will help create a pool of trained caregivers residing in and around 12 Cantonments namely Barrackpore (West Bengal), Belgaum (Karnataka), Jhansi (Uttar Pradesh), Deolali, Khadki & Pune (Maharashtra), Secunderabad (Telangana), St. Thomas Mount (Tamil Nadu), Ambala (Haryana), Delhi, and Ferozepur & Jalandhar (Punjab).
A Joint Working Group comprising representatives of both Ministries will facilitate coordination, implementation and monitoring of the initiative.
The initiative assumes special significance as the Defence Estates Department embarks on its centenary celebrations, marking 100 years of institutional service since its establishment in 1926. The partnership reflects the Department’s evolving role in contributing not only to efficient municipal administration in cantonments but also to the broader social welfare of cantonment residents and communities.
The MoU represents a significant example of cooperation and synergy between two Ministries, translating the vision of a ‘Whole of Government’ approach into concrete action. By bringing together the institutional network and civic infrastructure of Cantonment Boards with the policy framework, technical expertise and financial support of MoSJE, the initiative seeks to maximise the utilisation of existing public resources.

The National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology (NIELIT), under the Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, successfully concluded the Day 1 of the
3rd National Conference on Cyber Security, Digital Forensics & Intelligence (NCCDFI 2026)
on 16 November 2026 at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi.
Day 1 of the NCCDFI 2026 under the theme
“Cyber Secure Bharat: Fortifying India's Digital Future,”
brought together policymakers, senior government officials, law enforcement agencies, defence personnel, judicial representatives, cybersecurity professionals, industry leaders, researchers and academicians to deliberate on the evolving cybersecurity landscape and the growing challenges of digital crime and investigations.
The conference was inaugurated by
Prof. (Dr.) M. M. Tripathi, Director General, National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology (NIELIT) & Honourable Vice-Chancellor, NIELIT Deemed to be University
, as the Chief Guest, in the august presence of distinguished dignitaries; Shri Rupin Sharma, IPS, DGP Nagaland; Dr. Sandeep Mittal, IPS, DGP & Chairman, TNUSRB, Government of Tamil Nadu; Ms. A. Pratibha, Economic Advisor, MeitY; Shri Sridhar CV, Mission Director, Andhra Pradesh State Quantum Mission (APSQM), GoAP;  Shri Atul Tripathi, Honorary Adjunct Fellow at National Maritime Foundation and Shri L Lanuwabang, Director, NIELIT Kohima.
The inaugural session of the
3rd National Conference on Cyber Security, Digital Forensics & Intelligence (NCCDFI 2026)
commenced with a welcome address by Shri L Lanuwabang, that had set the tone for the two-day national conference. The welcome note highlighted NCCDFI's journey from Kohima (2024) to Guwahati (2025) and New Delhi (2026), acknowledging the leadership of Prof. (Dr.) M. M. Tripathi, Director General, NIELIT. He emphasised on the need for collective action, institutional collaboration and innovation to address emerging cyber threats. The conference spreads over seven technical sessions, over 30 speakers and 12 industry partners, aiming to strengthen India's cybersecurity and digital forensics capabilities towards building a
Cyber Secure Bharat
.
In the inaugural address by Chief Guest,
Prof. (Dr.) M. M. Tripathi, Director General, National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology (NIELIT) & Honourable Vice-Chancellor, NIELIT Deemed to be University
, he emphasised that cybersecurity has evolved beyond IT into a critical national priority, encompassing law enforcement, banking stability, critical infrastructure, public trust and national security. He highlighted NIELIT's key initiatives, including
ICSAS, Live Website Acquisition Tool, Cyber Crime Management System and CyberDaksh
, an AI-powered assistant being developed to support cybercrime investigators. He also announced NIELIT Deemed-to-be University's initiative to establish a dedicated
Quantum and Artificial Intelligence University campus at Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh
, envisioned as a centre for advanced education, research and innovation in these emerging technologies. He emphasized upon three priorities:
PRIORITY 1 - BUILD OUR OWN TECHNOLOGY
- NIELIT's efforts to develop indigenous cybersecurity solutions, including ICSAS, Live Website Acquisition Tool, Cyber Crime Management System and CyberDaksh. He emphasised India's need to become a technology creator rather than merely a consumer, while strengthening capabilities in AI, semiconductors, electronics, digital forensics and other emerging technologies.
PRIORITY 2 - BUILD PEOPLE AND NATIONAL SKILLS -
NIELIT's role in addressing the national skill gap through industry-aligned education, specialised training and digital learning. Key initiatives include B.Tech, M.Tech and Ph.D. programmes, the proposed Quantum and AI University campus at Amaravati, NIELIT Digital University with over 3.70 lakh enrolments, and semiconductor ATMP training facilities in Ahmedabad and Guwahati. He also emphasised strengthening cybersecurity and digital forensics skills among police, judiciary, armed forces and government officials to build a future-ready workforce.
PRIORITY 3 - BUILD A STRONG NATIONAL ECOSYSTEM -
the importance of building a strong national cybersecurity ecosystem through collaboration among government agencies, law enforcement, academia and industry. He highlighted the signing of MoUs at NCCDFI 2026 to promote institutional partnerships and practical outcomes.
Shri Rupin Sharma, highlighted NCCDFI's journey from Kohima to Guwahati and New Delhi, appreciating NIELIT Kohima's support in strengthening Nagaland Police's cyber-forensic capabilities, specialised training and digital recruitment systems.
Dr. Sandeep Mittal, highlighted that human beings remain the weakest link in the cybersecurity ecosystem, whether they are end users, software developers or system administrators. He also congratulated NIELIT on organising a successful and insightful conference, and appreciated NIELIT's efforts in undertaking a large-scale Faculty Development Programme (FDP) across the country.
Ms. A. Pratibha, highlighted India's efforts to strengthen its cybersecurity ecosystem through large-scale skill development, institutional capacity building, and coordinated cyber threat response. She also stressed that technical expertise must be supported by ethics, privacy, and responsible technology practices to achieve
Cyber Secure Bharat, Viksit Bharat 2047, and Aatmanirbhar Bharat.
Shri Sridhar CV, highlighted the critical role of NIELIT in promoting cybersecurity awareness and capacity building across the country. He noted that NIELIT has trained more than 1.6 crore individuals, including a significant number in the domain of cybersecurity. He emphasised that while substantial investments are being made in developing digital infrastructure and advanced technologies, equal attention must be given to securing these assets by fostering a strong cybersecurity mindset.
Shri Atul Tripathi, in his address emphasized that cybersecurity begins with individual awareness and responsibility. In an increasingly interconnected world, our personal data, digital footprints, and online behaviour can become vulnerabilities exploited by cybercriminals and adversaries. Practising good cyber hygiene, protecting sensitive information, avoiding oversharing on social media, and creating awareness among vulnerable communities are essential to strengthening our collective security.
Dr. Alok Tripathi, Director (Scheme/Skilling), NIELIT, delivered the Vote of Thanks, expressing his gratitude to the distinguished dignitaries, eminent cybersecurity professionals, representatives from law enforcement agencies, academia and industry, speakers, researchers, delegates, members of the media and NIELIT colleagues for their valuable participation and contributions to the conference.
The conference witnessed the signing of MoUs between NIELIT and various partner organisations, marking a significant step towards fostering institutional and industry collaboration. The agreements seek to promote joint research, technology development, specialised training and knowledge sharing in cybersecurity and related emerging technology domains. The organisations with which MoUs were exchanged are Bhasha Interface for India (BHASHINI); Anuvadini – AI-Based Translation Platform, InGage Technologies, QuNu Labs Private Limited, IBM India, Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University Hyderabad (JNTUH), and Pan IIT Alumni Foundation.
The conference also witnessed the launch of new digital applications by NIELIT viz.
CyberVitals
and
Net
अन्वेषक
; and kick-off of
Cyber Kushti 2026 – Cybersecurity & AI Hackathon
, aimed at fostering innovation, practical problem-solving and technical excellence among aspiring cybersecurity professionals through challenges centred on
Review, Attack and Defend
.
CyberVitals
mobile app is a cybersecurity and privacy suite that detects risky permissions, malware, unsafe app sources, outdated apps, and potential security threats. It also analyzes images for AI-generated content and provides trust scores for better verification. Real-time network, app activity, and notification monitoring helps identify suspicious behaviour while keeping user data private.
Net
अन्वेषक
,
the Network Explorer developed by NIELIT Gorakhpur is an in-house Network Administration Suite for device discovery, network monitoring, security assessment and diagnostics through a single application. It also offers tools for port scanning, PC security analysis, uptime monitoring and network troubleshooting.
An industry exhibition was also organised as part of the conference, showcasing advanced technologies, products and solutions in cybersecurity, digital forensics, drone technology, surveillance systems and AI-driven security. 12 industry partners along with knowledge partners, showcased innovative technologies, products and solutions in cybersecurity and digital forensics. The exhibition facilitated technology demonstrations, networking and collaboration among industry stakeholders, experts and delegates.  The exhibitors include, Telangana Cyber Security Bureau, ADF Solutions, Vertexon Labs, Stellar, 4n6care Technologies Pvt. Ltd., 3rd Eye Techno Solutions, MSAB, Magnet Forensics, CyberPeace, Cellebrite, ISAC, and Forensicsguru, besides NIELIT Ropar (NDU) & NIELIT Deemed to be University, NIELIT Kohima and NIELIT Gorakhpur.  The exhibition provided an interactive platform for technology demonstrations, knowledge exchange and networking among industry partners, government agencies, students and other stakeholders.
The conference featured a series of technical sessions, expert talks and panel discussions covering critical areas such as Artificial Intelligence-driven cyber threats, digital forensics, critical infrastructure protection, cyber intelligence, incident response, blockchain security, cloud security, digital evidence, cyber law and emerging technologies. Experts from government agencies, law enforcement, defence establishments, academia and the technology industry shared their insights, experiences and perspectives on addressing contemporary cybersecurity challenges.
Through this platform, NIELIT reaffirms its commitment to support the Government of India's vision of a secure, resilient and digitally empowered nation.
