title: India calls for Country-Driven Just Transition Mechanism at COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye); Emphasizes Adequate Finance, Technology Transfer and Capacity Building for Developing Countries
subtitle:
Shri Bhupender Yadav calls for a Two-tier, Party-guided Mechanism that respects National Sovereignty and diverse National Circumstances

India stresses that Just Transition must address Employment, Social Protection, Adaptation, Poverty Eradication and Energy Access
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 NOV 2026 8:23PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today called for moving the global just transition agenda from dialogue and exchange of experiences towards practical, country-driven implementation. Addressing the Fourth Annual High-Level Ministerial Roundtable on Just Transition under the UAE Just Transition Work Programme at UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye), the Minister reiterated India's commitment to an inclusive and equitable global transition that leaves no one behind.
Presented India's views at the 4th Annual High-level Ministerial Roundtable on Just Transition on the sidelines of COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye today.

Underlined the need to integrate just transition considerations across adaptation, livelihoods and development planning.

India supports the operationalisation of a two-tier, Party-guided Mechanism, responsive to developing-country needs and respectful of national sovereignty and diverse national circumstances.
— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp)
November 16, 2026
Shri Yadav emphasised that just transition must follow a whole-of-economy and whole-of-society approach, addressing employment, social protection, adaptation, poverty eradication, energy access and sustainable development. He highlighted that adequate financial support, technology transfer and capacity-building are essential to enable developing countries to implement their national priorities.
Noting that there can be no one-size-fits-all approach, he cited India's sub-national heat action and disaster management plans, which address vulnerabilities of workers and communities, as well as the country's renewable energy expansion that seeks to combine low-carbon development with affordable energy access. These examples underline the need to integrate just transition considerations across adaptation, livelihoods and development planning, he added.
The Minister underlined the need for clearly defined and complementary roles for the UAE Just Transition Work Programme and the proposed Just Transition Mechanism. While the Work Programme should continue to provide a platform for dialogue and exchange of experiences, the Mechanism should facilitate practical support through technical assistance, capacity-building and cooperation, translating the learnings from ongoing discussions into action, he stated.
Reaffirming India's support for operationalising a two-tier, Party-guided Just Transition Mechanism, Shri Yadav stressed that it must be responsive to the needs of developing countries and respectful of national sovereignty and diverse national circumstances. The Mechanism should build on existing efforts, avoid duplication and facilitate access to adequate means of implementation. It must neither prescribe uniform sectoral pathways nor create new obligations, but enable countries to pursue their own just transition pathways in accordance with national priorities, while ensuring that workers, communities and vulnerable groups are not left behind, the Minister stressed.
Shri Yadav observed that COP31 presents an important opportunity to move from exchanging experiences to practical, country-driven implementation. India stands ready to work constructively with all Parties towards an inclusive outcome that advances just transition while safeguarding the developmental priorities of developing countries, the Minister concluded.

content:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addressed the Ramoji Excellence Awards Ceremony – 2026 in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh. On the occasion, Governor of Andhra Pradesh Shri S. Abdul Nazeer, Chief Minister Shri Chandrababu Naidu, Union Ministers Shri G. Kishan Reddy and Shri K. Ram Mohan Naidu, Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh Shri K. Pawan Kalyan, and several other dignitaries were present.
Addressing the award ceremony, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that today marks the 90th birth anniversary of Ramoji Rao, who is no longer among us. He said that there are individuals who, through their dedicated work during their lifetime, evolve into institutions, and the institutions they establish continue to inspire the nation forever. Shri Shah said that he had met Ramoji Rao on four occasions and he remained well-informed about developments from every corner of the country. He had a clear understanding of every problem facing the nation and its possible solutions. He held firm convictions of his own and had the courage to express them fearlessly and candidly. He said that Ramoji Rao had an excellent understanding of ground realities. He said that Ramoji Rao continues to serve as a role model for young people in several fields, including agriculture, education, filmmaking and media.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Ramoji Rao had an in-depth understanding of the geographical situation, population, challenges and root causes of insurgency in the Northeast. Shri Amit Shah said more he came to know about Ramoji Rao, the greater his respect for him became.
Shri Amit Shah said that when one looks back at the 90-year life of Ramoji Rao, it becomes evident that hardly anyone else could have made such an extensive contribution to the nation across so many fields. He said that Ramoji Rao was born into a poor family in Krishna district and had no inheritance, resources or formal degree in journalism. However, he possessed vision in his eyes and mind, along with unwavering determination. Shri Shah said that by launching the newspaper
Eenadu
, Ramoji Rao sought to make the voice of truth resonate among readers. He said that if Ramoji Rao's contribution were to be assessed today, it could be said that in the world of journalism, the only media group chairman with whom he could be compared was Ram Nath Goenka.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Ramoji Rao always kept pace with changing times and evolving technology. He said that when private news channels were first introduced, no one other than Ramoji Rao could have envisioned the possibility of running 24-hour news channels in regional languages. Shri Shah said that Ramoji Rao launched ETV not only in Telugu but also in almost all the regional languages of the country. He added that Ramoji Rao not only enriched the country's regional languages but also took the innovative initiative of making the voice of truth resonate among people across the country through the ETV network.
Shri Amit Shah said that on one occasion, when he asked Ramoji Rao what he wished to accomplish with the time he had left, the latter had replied that he wanted to launch a TV channel on mobile phones. He said that today, his mobile channels are available in all languages. It is this passion to keep contributing and the zeal to constantly strive and overcome challenges that make Ramoji Rao truly great.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that when we look at the owners of today's newspapers and news channels, their business objectives and their focus on profits, we realise what a towering personality Ramoji Rao was. Shri Shah said that Ramoji Rao must have firmly believed that journalism, in its true sense, constitutes the fourth pillar of democracy. He made numerous sacrifices and faced many struggles throughout his life to uphold this conviction.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Ramoji Rao spent two major phases of his life in struggle. Despite significant financial losses and numerous challenges, he maintained the impartiality of his news channel and upheld its role as a true fourth pillar of democracy. Shri Shah said that those who struggle to build their careers are also great individuals. Struggle is a unique quality that makes a person great. However, those who struggle to uphold values are even greater. Ramoji Rao always fought for values and worked to establish them.
Shri Amit Shah said that when Ramoji Rao was conferred the Padma Vibhushan in 2016, a renowned Gujarati newspaper from Gujarat had written that the honour was not merely a recognition of Ramoji Rao, but also an honour for journalism, literature, education and Telugu pride. Shri Shah said that Ramoji Rao had not merely built a news industry; he had created institutions rather than businesses. Institutions are those that continue to function and uphold the same values even after their founders are no longer present.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Ramoji Rao also made significant contributions to the film industry. He said that it is difficult to imagine the film industry of any language without Ramoji Film City. Shri Shah said that Ramoji Rao assured filmmakers that if they came with the funds and their creative vision, everything else would be available at his studio, and they would not need to go anywhere else.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that several individuals have been selected for the Excellence Awards this year. People who have made significant contributions to the nation in fields such as science and technology, young icons, service to humanity, art and culture, education, medicine and healthcare, rural development, journalism and women's achievements are being honoured on this occasion. He said that he would like to tell all nine award recipients, who are being recognised for their contributions in these nine fields crucial to the country's development, that they may receive many more awards in their lives, but an award associated with the name of Ramoji Rao holds a special significance of its own.
Shri Amit Shah said that under the able leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India is moving forward on the path of progress. He said that over the past 13 years, the country has witnessed stability, continuity and decisive leadership after a long period. The era when policy paralysis was widely discussed has now given way to performance-driven politics and development based on sound policies. Union Home Minister said that significant progress has been made in several areas, including the abrogation of Article 370, ending the five-decade-old problem of Naxalism, driving the country's economic growth and ensuring national security. He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India's economy is advancing rapidly, while opportunities are expanding at an equally fast pace across all sectors.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that despite the prolonged wars between Russia and Ukraine, and between the United States and other countries, positive projections have emerged regarding India's economic growth.  Moody’s has recently raised its growth forecast for India for 2026–27 from 6.5% to 7%. In 2025–26, India recorded exports worth a record USD 863 billion, and our next target is USD 1 trillion. He expressed confidence that we would achieve this target.
Shri Shah said that India has become the world's second-largest producer in the manufacturing sector. India now produces more steel than the United States and Japan combined. This achievement has been accomplished over the past 12 years. He further said that earlier, only 58 Gram Panchayats had internet connectivity, whereas today, 2 lakh 15 thousands Gram Panchayats have been connected through 4G services, accounting for approximately 98 per cent of the total Gram Panchayats.
Shri Amit Shah said that India has made significant progress in the economic sector as well. The world's longest and highest-capacity hydrogen train has been built in India using completely indigenous technology, and its operations have also commenced.
He said that in 2014, the country had only 76 airports, whereas today, India has made significant strides, with the number of airports reaching 150. Shri Shah further said that, according to a World Bank report, during the 12 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's tenure, 50 crore Indians have come out of poverty, which is a matter of great satisfaction for everyone.

date:

                16 NOV 2026 5:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Self-Enumeration (SE) process for Phase II of Census 2027 i.e. Population Enumeration (PE) has commenced today in the States of Goa, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and the non-snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand. Residents can submit their household details online till November 30, 2026.
The corresponding house-to-house Population Enumeration in these States and areas will be conducted from December 1, 2026 to January 4, 2027 followed by a revisional round from January 5 to 9, 2027. The reference date for these States/areas will be 00:00 hours of January 5, 2027.
In the remaining States and Union Territories, Population Enumeration will be conducted from January 25 to February 28, 2027 followed by a revisional round from March 1 to 5, 2027. The provision for Self-Enumeration in these States/UTs will be available from January 10 to 24, 2027, prior to the commencement of house-to-house visits by Enumerators. The reference date for Census in these States/UTs will be 00:00 hours of March 1, 2027.
The Houselisting and Housing Census (HLO) under Phase I of Census 2027 have been completed across 35 States and Union Territories, except Manipur, marking the completion of first phase of the Census exercise.
For the first time, Census 2027 is being conducted using digital tools, with Self-Enumeration introduced as an additional facility. It is a secure, convenient and user-friendly web-based facility available in 16 Indian languages. To participate in Self-Enumeration during Phase II, residents can log in to the official portal
se.census.gov.in
using their mobile number (preferably the one registered during Phase I) along with basic details and answer 40 notified questions covering household and individual particulars. Upon successful submission, a unique Self-Enumeration ID (SE ID) is generated, which is to be shared with the Enumerator during the subsequent field visit to complete the process.
While Self-Enumeration allows residents to provide their details online at their convenience, Enumerators will continue to carry out door-to-door visits in all allocated blocks. Households that do not opt for Self-Enumeration will be covered during the house-to-house visits by Enumerators.
All information collected under the Census Act, 1948, remains strictly confidential and is used solely for statistical purposes and development planning. Residents are encouraged to actively participate in this important national exercise and extend their cooperation to Enumerators.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah, today addressed the unveiling ceremony of statue of Maharashtra’s former Deputy Chief Minister, Ajit Pawar, in Pune. title: Delhi's Waste Landmark Gets a Remarkable Second Life, Patel Chest Turns Waste into Wonder
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 NOV 2026 3:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Breathing new life into a forgotten space through circularity and community engagement, Patel Chest in Delhi – a dhalao ghar until recently has been re-imagined as an RRR Centre, under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0.
For years, a corner near Delhi University's Patel Chest was known for only one thing, waste. The old Dhalao Ghar served as a collection point for garbage, a place people passed by without a second glance. But under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0, that forgotten space was destined for a remarkable second life.
In a unique transformation led by DMSWSL in association with MCD Civil Lines Zone, the abandoned waste collection site was reimagined as an RRR (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle) Centre and Selfie Point. What was once a symbol of disposal, became a celebration of sustainability.
The makeover itself told a powerful story. Around 45 discarded tyres and more than 3,000 used bricks were creatively repurposed to build an attractive public space. Materials once considered waste were transformed into colourful installations, proving that with creativity and purpose, yesterday's discards can become tomorrow's landmarks.
Today, students walking through Delhi University stop not to avoid the site, but to admire it. The vibrant Selfie Point attracts visitors, sparking conversations about sustainability and encouraging people to rethink the value of items they often throw away.
Beside it stands the RRR Centre, where citizens donate unused clothes, books, toys, and e-waste. Instead of ending up in landfills, these items are channelled towards reuse, refurbishment, and responsible recycling, extending their life and benefiting the community.
The transformation is more than a facelift. It is a living lesson in the circular economy, where waste is not an end point but the beginning of something new.
Today, the former Dhalao Ghar stands as a reminder that change is possible. A place once associated with waste now inspires action, awareness, and participation.
Because in the spirit of Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0, even a waste collection point can become a destination, a conversation starter, and a symbol of how cities can turn waste into worth.
Every discarded item has a story left to tell. At Patel Chest, Delhi, those stories have found a new stage.

title: 10 Films to Compete for ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal at 57th IFFI
subtitle: Four-member international jury headed by Dr. Prof. Ahmed Bedjaoui to adjudicate the entries
content:
Goa, 16 November 2026
Ten Indian and international fiction feature films will compete for the prestigious ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), scheduled to be held in Goa from 20th to 28th November, 2026. The selected films explore themes of peace, tolerance, empathy, social justice and intercultural dialogue, in keeping with the festival's overarching theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’.
Instituted at the 46th edition of IFFI in collaboration with the International Council for Film, Television and Audiovisual Communication (CICT-ICFT), Paris, under the aegis of UNESCO, the award recognizes films that reflect Mahatma Gandhi's ideals of non-violence, tolerance, intercultural understanding and a culture of peace.
The four-member international jury will be headed by Prof. (Dr.) Ahmed Bedjaoui of Algeria, a University professor, filmmaker, producer and film critic. The other members are Maria Cristina Iglesias of Argentina/France, former Head of Programme at UNESCO's Cultural Sector; Georges Dupont of Luxembourg, former Director-General of CICT-ICFT; and Manouj Kadaamh of India, an internationally acclaimed filmmaker and member of ICFT.
The ten films selected for this year's competition bring together stories from diverse cultural backgrounds, highlighting human relationships, social challenges and shared values.
The international line-up includes
Call Me Queen
, directed by Emily Atef, a Germany-France-UK-Kenya production set in 1990s Nairobi. It follows a single mother who finds strength in an unexpected friendship while confronting an AIDS diagnosis and social injustice. The film will have its India Premiere at IFFI.
India is represented by three films.
Kabir Sir ka Akhri Lesson (Kabir Sir)
, directed by Sarfaraz Alam and starring Vinay Pathak, explores the challenges faced by veteran educators in the age of technology and will have its World Premiere.
Scroll
, directed by Kannan S, examines smartphone addiction through the disturbing experiences of a young man using an app-based game to control his screen time.
Sev Micchar
, the debut feature of Muskan Asthana, explores family tensions, rivalry and reconciliation through the story of a shopkeeper facing financial and personal challenges.
The Haiti-France-Belgium-Luxembourg-Canada production
Marie Madeleine
, directed by Gessica Généus, explores faith, social conventions and personal freedom through the evolving relationship between an independent woman and a young evangelist. The film won the Grand Prix du Jury at the Festival de Cabourg 2026 and will have its Asia Premiere at IFFI.
Ghanaian-American filmmaker Amartei Armar's
Our Time Will Come (Ego Reach We All)
follows two orphans travelling to Accra in search of their last living parent. The film won the Pardo for Change and Pardo for Best Performance at the Locarno Film Festival 2026 and will have its Asia Premiere.
Turkish filmmaker Faysal Soysal's
Rahma
tells the story of an archaeologist whose unexpected bond with a nine-year-old Syrian orphan brings emotional healing and changes her outlook on life. The film will have its Asia Premiere.
Strawberries (La más dulce)
, directed by Laïla Marrakchi, follows two Moroccan women working as seasonal strawberry pickers in Spain who find the courage to stand against workplace abuse and exploitation. The France-Morocco-Spain-Belgium production will have its India Premiere.
Another Turkish entry,
The Farm
(Süt Çiftliği), directed by Elif Eda, follows a 12-year-old girl who, disturbed by the separation of newborn calves from their mothers at a dairy farm, joins an orphaned veterinary apprentice to free the pregnant cows. The film will have its International Premiere at IFFI.
The Taiwan-Singapore production,
Will You Still Be My Friend
(
Ri guang
), directed by Lu Po-Shun, explores the friendship between two 13-year-old boys from different backgrounds, as tensions among adults threaten to drive them apart. The film will have its India Premiere.
Through this diverse selection, the ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal competition at the 57th IFFI brings together cinematic narratives that promote compassion, mutual respect, peaceful coexistence and shared human values across cultures and geographical boundaries.

title: Marathi Cinema Takes Centre Stage at 57th IFFI
subtitle: Diverse film selections accompany special tributes to Legends Suryakant Mandhare and Nana Patekar
content:
Goa, 16 November 2026
Mumbai, the heart of India’s mainstream Hindi film industry, is also home to a vibrant Marathi cinema tradition that has evolved alongside Bollywood, carving out a distinct identity through its rich content driven storytelling, grounded realism, and deep literary roots. Celebrating this enduring cinematic legacy, the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) brings the diversity of Marathi cinema into focus through a selection of contemporary feature and non-feature films, alongside tributes to its celebrated personalities and cinematic heritage.
This year at IFFI, seven Marathi films have been selected for the Indian Panorama, while a celebrated classic will be presented in its restored version under the Centenary Tributes section. Another Marathi film will be showcased under the Gala Premieres section.
Among the feature-film selections,
Aadi Anant
, directed by Mahesh Limaye, explores the emotional bond between an aspiring actor and his grandfather. The film which highlights the challenges of caregiving, family responsibilities and the meaning of success, features Ashok Saraf, Sankarshan Karhade, Sakhi Gokhale and Yogesh Shirsat.
The Mainstream Cinema section of Indian Panorama brings together
Deool Band 2 (Temple Closed 2)
, written and directed by Pravin Vitthal Tarde, which portrays agrarian distress through the story of a woman who loses her farmer husband and
Baapya (The Man)
, directed by Samir Tewari, that  follows a transgender protagonist returning to their hometown, weaving together themes of family and gender identity.
Another notable selection is
Tighee
, directed by Jeejivisha Kale, which is among the films featured in the Best Debut Director of Indian Feature Film category at IFFI.
This poignant family drama delves into relationships, sacrifice and the pain of unspoken emotions.
The Indian Panorama non-feature section further showcases three Marathi films, each offering a distinct narrative. Amyth Patkar’s
Punishment (Shiksha)
examines guilt and its consequences through two seemingly unrelated thefts. Santosh Davakhar’s
Sky Tree (Abhal-Vriksh)
portrays a villager’s hopes amid drought, while Nipun Dharmadhikari’s
The Moon (Chandoba)
captures a teenager’s struggle with vitiligo and the social judgement surrounding the condition.
Beyond the Indian Panorama selections,
Tu Aahes Na (You Are There, Right?)
, directed by National Award-winning filmmaker Deepak Gawade, will be presented under the Gala Premieres section. The film touches upon grief, loneliness and identity, highlighting the unexpected human connections that bring meaning to life.
Marathi storytelling also finds a place in IFFI’s Best Web Series Award category through
Devkhel
, directed by Chandrakanth Lata Gaikwad. This gripping crime thriller is set in a coastal village where a series of mysterious ritual-linked murders unfold, with superstition concealing a chilling truth.
The festival also celebrates Marathi cinema’s rich legacy through the Centenary Tributes section, commemorating legendary actor Suryakant Mandhare on his birth centenary. As part of the tribute, his 1965 Marathi film
Sadhi Manase
will be presented in its restored version by the National Film Archive of India (NFAI) under the National Film Heritage Mission. A Homage section dedicated to the late Nana Patekar, renowned for his intense and memorable performances in Hindi and Marathi cinema, is also part of the 57th IFFI. The screening of his Hindi film
Diksha
and open air screening of his iconic Marathi film
Natsamrat
at Miramar Beach will offer audiences an opportunity to celebrate the legendary actor’s enduring contribution to Indian cinema.

title: Journalism Must Balance Freedom of Expression with Responsibility; Media Must Adapt to Rapid Technological Changes: Union Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw
subtitle:
“Less Noise, More News; Less Sensationalism, More Responsibility”: Shri Rajat Sharma

PCI Chairperson Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai Emphasises Ethical, Accurate and Responsible Journalism

AI Can Assist Journalism, but Editorial Judgement and Accountability Must Remain Human: Secretary, I&B

Press Council of India Releases 2026 Edition of Norms of Journalistic Conduct
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 NOV 2026 5:00PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Information & Broadcasting, Railways and Electronics & Information Technology, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, addressed the National Press Day celebrations organised by the Press Council of India at Rangbhawan Auditorium, Akashvani Bhawan, New Delhi, today.
Underlining the vital role of media in strengthening democracy, he called upon media professionals to adapt to the rapidly evolving media landscape and technological advancements. He underscored the importance of upholding responsible journalism and the media
’
s responsibility towards society.
The event was attended by PCI Chairperson Justice (Retd.) Ranjana Prakash Desai; Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, Shri Chanchal Kumar; renowned journalist Shri Rajat Sharma, who delivered the keynote address and
PCI Member Dr. Sudhanshu Trivedi.This year’s theme,
“Journalism: Populist or Responsible”
, highlighted the evolving role of journalism in an era of rapid information dissemination and growing digital influence.
Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw Calls for Collective Efforts to Empower Citizens and Strengthen Society
Addressing the gathering, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw highlighted the unprecedented pace of technological transformation, observing that the next five years could witness changes greater than those experienced over the previous two decades. He encouraged young journalists to embrace change and continuously upgrade their skills.
Emphasising accountability of digital platforms, he raised significant questions over whether community guidelines are enough in the face of increasing misinformation, deepfakes, misleading advertisements, digital arrests and harmful content affecting children. He stressed the need to deliberate on how this changing media landscape be governed to empower citizens and address emerging challenges.
Shri Rajat Sharma Underscores the Thin Line Between Sensationalism and Responsibility
Delivering the keynote address, Shri Rajat Sharma emphasized that there is a thin line between sensationalism and responsibility, foregrounding the importance of editorial judgement and responsible reporting. Recalling experiences from the Emergency, the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks and Operation Sindoor, he highlighted the need for restraint, verification and sensitivity, particularly while reporting on matters of national security.
Calling for greater accountability in the digital media ecosystem, he urged journalists to prioritise accuracy over sensationalism, concluding with the message:
“Less Noise, More News; Less Sensationalism, More Responsibility.”
PCI Chairperson Reaffirms Commitment to Press Freedom and Journalistic Standards
PCI Chairperson Justice (Retd.) Ranjana Prakash Desai reaffirmed the Council’s commitment to protecting press freedom and improving journalistic standards. Underlining the rapid transformation in the media landscape, she observed that technological advancements have made information accessible to millions within seconds. She observed that anyone with a phone and internet connection can now become a news disseminator, but not everyone reporting the news is trained in or bound by journalistic ethics.
Shri Chanchal Kumar Emphasises Accuracy, Editorial Judgement and Human Accountability in the Age of AI
Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, Shri Chanchal Kumar, emphasised that journalism must strike a balance between public engagement and credibility. He observed that popularity must not take precedence over truth, nor should virality outweigh verification. Highlighting the growing influence of TRPs, clicks and digital engagement, he stressed the importance of editorial judgement, fact-checking and distinguishing news from opinion. He underlined that AI can assist journalism but cannot assume the responsibility of a journalist.
PCI Member and Rajya Sabha MP Dr. Sudhanshu Trivedi called for critical examination of international indices and emphasised that integrity and the responsible dissemination of information are essential as India progresses towards a new direction of development.
P
CI Releases 2026 Edition of Norms of Journalistic Conduct
A key highlight of the celebrations was the release of the
2026 Edition of the Norms of Journalistic Conduct
by the Press Council of India, incorporating updated guidelines on:
•  Reporting during natural disasters and conflict situations.
•  Coverage of protests and demonstrations.
•  Reporting on sex workers and persons with disabilities.
•  Protection of children
’
s privacy.
•  Advertisements relating to online money games, in line with the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025.
A
bout Press Council of India
The Press Council of India was set up by an Act of Parliament as a quasi-judicial authority in 1966 and re-established in 1979, with the objective of providing an internal self-regulatory mechanism for the print media to ensure free and responsible reporting. Since its inception, the Council has consistently strived to protect and preserve the freedom of the press and raise the standards of newspapers and news agencies in the country.

title: Ministry of Minority Affairs Organises Workshop on AI for Digital Transformation to Strengthen AI-Enabled Governance

                16 NOV 2026 5:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Minority Affairs organised a one-day workshop on ‘AI for Digital Transformation,’ in collaboration with the Wadhwani Government AI Academy, on 16th November, 2026, to familiarise senior officials with the evolving AI landscape and explore its potential to transform public administration. The workshop was chaired by Dr. Srivatsa Krishna, Secretary, Ministry of Minority Affairs, and was attended by senior officials of the Ministry.
The programme focused on the ongoing emphases towards AI-enabled governance, highlighting the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Generative AI and Agentic AI in enhancing administrative processes and institutional efficiency.
Addressing the inaugural session, Dr. Srivatsa Krishna emphasised the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence and the need for government institutions to proactively understand and embrace its applications. Drawing a parallel with the advent of the internet, he described AI as a defining technological shift that would have a far-reaching impact on society.
Highlighting the importance of practical learning over theoretical discussions, Dr. Krishna emphasised that the workshop should provide officers with hands-on exposure to AI tools, their applications and potential limitations, including the risks of AI-generated inaccuracies or hallucinations. He encouraged participants to actively engage with experts, raise questions and understand how these technologies could be responsibly leveraged in government functioning.
The workshop featured expert-led sessions, interactive discussions, hands-on exercises and demonstrations of AI-powered tools and agentic workflows. The sessions covered practical applications of AI in research, information extraction, document processing, administrative decision-making and other government functions. Participants also gained insights into the effective and responsible use of these tools in public administration.
The capacity-building programme is being undertaken in phases to facilitate wider participation across different levels of the Ministry's administrative hierarchy. Following the session for senior management, a dedicated programme for officials below the rank of Deputy Secretary is scheduled for 18th November, 2026. A more detailed follow-up workshop is also envisaged in December 2026 to further strengthen practical understanding and application of AI tools.
This initiative reflects the Ministry's commitment to institutional capacity building, administrative modernisation and the adoption of emerging technologies. Through structured learning opportunities and practical exposure, the Ministry aims to equip its officials with the knowledge and capabilities required to harness artificial Intelligence for more efficient, responsive and citizen-centric governance.

title: Along Goa’s Coastline, NH-66 Brings Together Connectivity, Development and Natural Beauty
subtitle: The 7.74-km Canacona Bypass in South Goa showcases how highway infrastructure connects communities while traversing the scenic landscapes of the Konkan coast
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 NOV 2026 4:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A journey along National Highway 66 (NH-66) in South Goa offers more than connectivity between destinations. Against the backdrop of rivers, forest cover and the Arabian Sea, the highway takes motorists through some of the most picturesque landscapes of the Konkan coast. The Canacona Bypass, in particular, brings together modern road infrastructure and the natural beauty of coastal Goa.
As the highway crosses the Galgibag, Talpona and Maxem rivers through three bridges, it offers striking views of shimmering waters, green landscapes and the coastline. Near Galgibaga Beach, the confluence of the river and coastal landscape adds to the scenic character of this stretch, making the journey as memorable as the destination.
Canacona Bypass: Strengthening Regional Connectivity
Developed under aegis of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH), the 7.74-km, four-lane Canacona Bypass, operational since 2019, connects Char Rasta to Mashem in South Goa. An important section of NH-66, the bypass improves connectivity through the Canacona region and provides a convenient route for commuters, local residents and visitors.
By facilitating the movement of people and goods, the bypass supports local businesses, livelihoods and access to important destinations. Its three river bridges are key components of this infrastructure, ensuring uninterrupted movement across waterways while offering expansive views of the surrounding landscape.
NH-66: A Major Highway Along India's Western Coast
The Canacona Bypass forms part of NH-66, one of India's major coastal highways, extending approximately 1,600 km from Panvel in Maharashtra to Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu. Traversing five states—Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu—the highway connects important towns, commercial centres, ports and tourist destinations along the western seaboard.
Running broadly parallel to the Arabian Sea and the Western Ghats, NH-66 serves as an important corridor for passenger and freight movement. It facilitates the transportation of agricultural produce, fisheries and industrial goods, linking local businesses and producers with wider markets. Its connectivity to commercial centres and ports also supports trade, tourism and regional economic activity.
A Highway Through Diverse Landscapes
From Panvel, NH-66 traverses Maharashtra's Konkan region, passing through Pen, Mahad, Chiplun and Ratnagiri before entering Goa. It connects key destinations such as Panaji and Margao before continuing towards Karnataka through Karwar, Udupi and Mangaluru.
Further south, the highway passes through Kerala's Kannur, Kozhikode, Kochi, Alappuzha, Kollam and Thiruvananthapuram, before reaching Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu, where it connects with NH-44.
Along this route, the landscape changes from river estuaries and forested hills to beaches, fishing settlements and bustling commercial centres. These varied surroundings reflect the geographical and cultural diversity of India's western coastline and the communities connected by this highway.
Infrastructure Connecting People and Places
The Canacona Bypass reflects how highway development goes beyond improving road connectivity. By facilitating smoother movement, supporting economic activities and connecting communities, such infrastructure contributes to regional development while serving the everyday needs of road users.
On Goa's NH-66, bridges across rivers, stretches of greenery and views of the Arabian Sea add a distinctive dimension to the journey. The Canacona Bypass thus stands as an example of how highway infrastructure can strengthen connectivity while taking travellers through the natural landscapes that define India's western coast.

India and Belarus took an important step towards strengthening their bilateral scientific and technological partnership with the signing of the Second Programme of Cooperation (PoC) for the period 2027–2029 between the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) of India, and the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus (NASB) at New Delhi on 16
th
November 2026.
The Programme of Cooperation was signed during a meeting between Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, Director General, CSIR and Secretary, DSIR, and Dr. A. V. Trukhanov, Deputy Chairman of the Presidium of NASB, who is visiting India from 15–18 November 2026 in connection with the 12th Meeting of the Belarusian-Indian Intergovernmental Commission on Cooperation in Economy, Trade, Industry, Science, Technology and Culture and the India-Belarus Business Forum.
The signing of the Second PoC builds upon the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Scientific and Technical Cooperation signed between CSIR and NASB on 22 May 2023. Under the first Programme of Cooperation (2024–2026), the two institutions launched a Joint Call for Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) proposals in October 2024, resulting in the approval seven joint projects.These projects are currently progressing through their second year of implementation.
The Second Programme of Cooperation (2027–2031) provides a renewed framework for expanding bilateral scientific collaboration, facilitating joint research and development initiatives and strengthening linkages between research institutions and scientists of both countries. It is expected to provide an impetus to collaborative research, technology development, knowledge exchange and innovation-driven partnerships through focused cooperation in mutually identified areas of science and technology.
As a key initiative under the Second Programme of Cooperation, CSIR and NASB propose to launch the Second Joint Call for Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Proposals from 27 November 2026 inviting proposals from researchers and scientists of both countries for undertaking collaborative research projects in mutually identified priority areas. The call is expected to provide fresh impetus to bilateral research partnerships, encourage scientific exchanges and facilitate the development of innovative solutions through joint research and technological collaboration.
Speaking on the occasion, Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, Director General, CSIR and Secretary, DSIR, highlighted the importance of sustained scientific partnerships in addressing emerging global challenges and advancing innovation-led development. The DG, CSIR emphasised the significant potential for Indian and Belarusian researchers to work together by leveraging their respective scientific strengths and institutional capabilities.
Dr. A. V. Trukhanov, Deputy Chairman of the Presidium of NASB, highlighted the importance of continued scientific engagement between India and Belarus and expressed interest in further strengthening institutional cooperation and expanding opportunities for joint research and technological collaboration, specifically through organizing Joint Laboratories between NASB and CSIR and exploring mechanisms to support cooperation activities targeting upscaling and translational research activities.
The signing of the Second Programme of Cooperation marks an important milestone in India–Belarus scientific relations. The renewed partnership is expected to further strengthen research collaboration, promote institutional linkages and create new opportunities for scientific exchange and innovation, contributing to the broader objectives of bilateral cooperation between the two countries.

content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, Dr. Jitendra Singh, visited the Trieste component of the "International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology" (ICGEB) in Italy, where he reviewed advanced research facilities and interacted with the Centre's leadership and Indian researchers, highlighting India's growing engagement in international biotechnology research, scientific training and technology development.
The Minister was welcomed by ICGEB Director-General Dr. Lawrence Banks, in the presence of members of the Indian delegation. During the visit, Dr. Jitendra Singh toured the Biotechnology Development Unit's biopharmaceutical production and training facility, the new Biosafety Level 3 laboratory and the Functional Cell Biology laboratory's high-throughput screening facility. He also held interactions with ICGEB leadership and Indian fellows at the Centre.
The visit provided an opportunity to highlight the significant contribution of ICGEB's India component to the country's biotechnology research and innovation ecosystem, particularly in areas aligned with India's BioE3 policy. The areas showcased included biobased chemicals and enzymes, climate-resilient agriculture, carbon capture and utilisation, precision biotherapeutics, and marine and space biomanufacturing.
Among the research initiatives highlighted for the visiting delegation were India's first biofoundry for microbial biomanufacturing, inaugurated by Dr. Jitendra Singh, research on enzyme and yeast systems for ethanol production, biological carbon capture, genome-edited crops and monoclonal antibodies against infectious diseases. These areas reflect the range of biotechnology research and technology development being undertaken through the ICGEB network in India.
The 'International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology' is an international, intergovernmental research organisation promoting excellence in advanced research, higher education, training and technology transfer in genetic engineering, biotechnology and life sciences. With its components in Trieste, New Delhi and Cape Town, ICGEB connects research, training and technology development across its international network.
India has a significant presence in ICGEB's activities, with the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India, supporting research and development programmes, innovation incubation and human resource development at the New Delhi component. The Centre's work in India encompasses frontier areas including molecular medicine, vaccines, diagnostics, plant biotechnology, bioenergy and genome editing technologies.
ICGEB New Delhi has also contributed to international scientific training and cooperation. Between 2023 and 2026, 67 researchers from 22 countries undertook or began training at the New Delhi component. This engagement has been complemented by workshops and scientific exchanges in areas including artificial intelligence in biology, drug development, genome editing, carbon capture, microscopy and flow cytometry.
Through its research, training and technology-transfer activities, ICGEB has also provided a platform for scientific collaboration with developing and emerging economies, including engagement with countries in Asia and Africa through joint research, training and technology transfer.
The visit brought into focus the importance of the India-ICGEB partnership in advancing biotechnology research, strengthening scientific capabilities and promoting the translation of research into applications in health, agriculture, industrial processes and environmental sustainability.
The programme also included a working lunch with Indian fellows at ICGEB, bringing together researchers, senior scientists and administrators of the Centre.

title: TDB-DST Signs Agreement with NeoSeeker Metals under RDI Fund to Advance Indigenous Critical Minerals Recovery Technology
subtitle: Advancing Indigenous Critical Minerals Recycling Technology from TRL-5 to TRL-9
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 NOV 2026 12:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
As India expands its footprint in electric mobility, clean energy, electronics and advanced manufacturing, the demand for critical minerals is set to grow significantly. This growing demand also brings into focus an important national challenge—securing access to these strategic resources sustainably while addressing the increasing volume of electronic and end-of-life battery waste.
Recognising this potential, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with M/s Neo Seekermetals Pvt. Ltd., Hyderabad, Telangana, under the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund. The agreement will support the development and commercialisation of an indigenous technology for the extraction of critical metals through the recycling of e-waste and lithium-ion battery waste.
The project, titled “Extraction of Critical Metals by Recycling of E-Waste and Lithium-Ion Battery Waste,” has a total project cost of ₹20 crore, with ₹10 crore approved under the RDI Fund. The financial assistance will be extended through Optionally Convertible Debt (OCD).
Neo Seekermetals is addressing this challenge through an integrated and patented recycling process designed to process both e-waste and lithium-ion battery waste. The technology seeks to recover valuable metals and battery materials from these complex waste streams, creating a pathway where materials that would otherwise be discarded can be brought back into the productive economy.
The project aims to advance the technology from Technology Readiness Level (TRL)-5 to TRL-9, taking it towards commercial-scale deployment. The proposed process is designed to support the recovery of a range of valuable materials, contributing to the development of a more resilient domestic ecosystem for critical minerals and metals.
Sh. Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, Technology Development Board, said,
“India's transition towards clean energy and advanced technologies will require secure and sustainable access to critical minerals. Developing indigenous capabilities to recover these resources from e-waste and end-of-life batteries is an important part of this larger effort. Through the RDI Fund, TDB is supporting technologies that can combine innovation with strategic relevance, helping transform waste streams into valuable resources and strengthening the foundations of a circular economy.”
An authorised representative of Neo Seekermetals said,
“The support from TDB under the RDI Fund will help us take our technology forward towards commercial deployment. Our focus is on building an efficient and sustainable process for recovering critical and valuable materials from e-waste and lithium-ion battery waste. This partnership will provide an important impetus to our efforts to build indigenous capabilities in resource recovery and contribute to India's growing circular economy.”

content:

:
Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) Sarbananda Sonowal
invited the global shipbuilders, shipping lines and financiers for investment as projections estimate nearly $10 billion of investment in the five new Greenfield coastal shipbuilding clusters, saying India aims to rank among the world's top 10 shipbuilding nations by 2030 and the top five by 2047.
Sonowal made the pitch at the India Shipbuilding Investment Conclave 2026, hosted by the MoPSW here today. He also launched Naukosh, a digital portal for the shipbuilding and ship repair industry, and the conclave saw Damen Shipyards and Cochin Shipyard sign a memorandum of understanding to collaborate on future shipbuilding projects.
"India is ready to build the ships of the world," Sarbananda Sonowal said. "Build in India, for India and for the world.” The conclave builds on the $8 billion shipbuilding financial package the government approved last year under Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal cited domestic and export demand as the case for investors. Identified domestic demand covers more than 400 vessels, representing an investment opportunity of nearly $24 billion, the minister said. The active order pipeline holds more than 150 vessels valued at over $1.7 billion, and export orders account for more than 80% of that value.
The investment push centers on five greenfield clusters that officials described as ready to build: Dugarajapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, Kuchhadi in Gujarat, Dighi in Maharashtra, Kendrapada in Odisha and Thoothukudi in Tamil Nadu. Central and state teams took investors through available land, supporting policies and joint Centre-state backing for shipyards, component makers and allied marine businesses.
Sonowal said the clusters would open opportunities in manufacturing, technology, employment and exports. “Under the dynamic leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, cooperative federalism is powering the next chapter of Make in India. Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Odisha and Tamil Nadu have shown that India’s coastal states are partners in this mission, not just hosts. We move this as Team India so that investors get land, approvals and policy support without delay,”
Sonowal
said.
Executives from 30 international shipyards joined shipping companies, equipment makers, banks, investors and diplomatic missions, along with Indian industry leaders. Among those taking part were HD KSOE, Samsung Heavy Industries, Hanwha Ocean, Fincantieri, Meyer Werft, Damen, Royal IHC, Everllence, Mitsui Engines, Wartsila, Kongsberg, Drydocks World Dubai, Maersk, MSC, CMA CGM, MOL and DP World.
The Korean Ambassador to India also led a large delegation after Union
Minister
Sarbananda Sonowal's recent visit to South Korea. HD KSOE, Samsung Heavy Industries and Hanwha Ocean are South Korea's three largest shipbuilders; shipping company HMM also attended. Their participation builds on VOYAGES, short for Vision for Operation of Yard Assisted Growth with Efficiency and Scale, the partnership PM Narendra Modi and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung signed April 2026 to pair Korean shipbuilding expertise with India's Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047.
Naukosh, developed by the ministry's Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA), brings policies, approvals and investment opportunities onto one digital platform, which Sarbananda Sonowal said would promote transparency and ease of doing business. It serves shipyards, repair facilities, equipment makers, design agencies, classification societies, research and training institutions, financiers, insurers and regulators.
Its modules cover an industry directory, shipyard capability data, a collaboration hub, finance and insurance information, a technical library, an innovation centre, training and certification, and regulatory guidance. A public homepage dashboard will show shipyard and capacity indicators, ships delivered and on order, and sector updates.
At a Global Maritime Leaders' Open House, executives gave government officials direct feedback on policy and long-term plans. Delegations then held one-on-one meetings with state cluster teams, central ministries and financial institutions to work toward specific deals. State governments have arranged site visits tomorrow (Tuesday on Nov. 17), for 10 international delegations to inspect the cluster locations.
"The participation of global leaders today reflects growing confidence in India as a shipbuilding destination," Sonowal said. "With assured demand, strong policy support, dedicated financing and five ready coastal clusters, India offers a compelling case for long-term investment. Our priority now is to convert today's discussions into projects on the ground."
Sonowal tied the effort to PM Modi's leadership, saying shipbuilding had become a pillar of the Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat journey. He said growth in the sector would create opportunities for Indian industries, enterprises and young people.

The Official said the cumulative sales of approximately ₹5.50 lakh recorded up to November 15, represent an encouraging development in the Ministry's efforts to promote market-oriented livelihood opportunities, that is also helping artisans enhance the visibility of their products and establish connections with a wider consumer base.

The initiative aims to create an enhanced platform for promoting artisan-made products and facilitating access to national and international markets, he added.
The Official said through TULIP, the Ministry seeks to connect traditional craftsmanship with contemporary consumer preferences and emerging market demands. The initiative also focuses on preserving India's artistic heritage while encouraging innovation, entrepreneurship and economic self-reliance among artisans.
He said the Ministry's participation in the Trade Fair demonstrates the importance of national-level exhibitions in expanding marketing opportunities for small entrepreneurs and traditional craftspeople.
The Official said the platforms enable artisans to showcase their capabilities, interact with potential customers, strengthen their market presence and explore opportunities for long-term business development.

By facilitating participation in prominent trade fairs and exhibitions, these Corporations are contributing to improved market access, increased product visibility and greater opportunities for income generation among their beneficiaries.
The Ministry's pavilion adds an important dimension of social and economic inclusion to IITF 2026 by bringing the products, skills and entrepreneurial potential of artisans from diverse social and geographical backgrounds into the mainstream marketplace.

Through initiatives such as TULIP and participation in national exhibitions, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment remains committed to strengthening sustainable livelihoods, promoting indigenous craftsmanship and advancing inclusive socio-economic development in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

title: From Alcohol Dependence to Financial Stability
subtitle:
A Journey of Recovery and Self-Reliance Through IRCA in Karnataka

Counselling, Therapeutic Interventions and Family Support Help 33-Year-Old Ramesh Gowda from Kolar Rebuild His Life

Ministry-Supported De-addiction Centre Helps Beneficiary Restore Family Relationships and Revive Business Activities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 NOV 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The journey of 33 year Ramesh Gowda
(name changed)
from alcohol dependence and financial difficulties towards improved well-being, stronger family relationships and renewed livelihood opportunities, offers an encouraging example of recovery supported by individual determination, professional counselling and family involvement.
Mr. Ramesh Gowda, a resident of Kolar district in Karnataka, has made significant progress towards recovery from alcohol dependence through counselling and rehabilitation assistance at the Alcohol and Drug Abuse Free De-addiction Centre, an Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA). His experience highlights the importance of timely professional support and family encouragement in rebuilding personal and professional life.
Belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC) community, Ramesh previously ran his own business. What began as occasional alcohol consumption gradually became regular amid family-related difficulties and stress. His growing dependence affected the management of his business, weakened financial stability and strained relationships with family members. Recognising these challenges and determined to improve his circumstances, he voluntarily approached the IRCA centre in Kolar for assistance. He received support beginning on January 6, 2024, including regular counselling, motivational guidance and therapeutic interventions designed to help him understand his personal goals and responsibilities.
The counselling process helped Ramesh reflect on the effects of alcohol dependence, strengthen his motivation and build confidence in pursuing recovery. The centre also conducted family counselling sessions to improve communication and understanding among family members and encourage a supportive environment for rehabilitation.
With sustained guidance and family support, Ramesh showed significant improvement in his behaviour and overall well-being. As his confidence returned, he was able to regain focus on his business activities and work towards greater financial stability.
The progress was also reflected in his family relationships. Improved communication and renewed attention to his responsibilities helped him rebuild healthier connections with his loved ones and pursue a more stable daily routine.
Following counselling and rehabilitation support, Ramesh has regained stability in his personal and professional life and is now earning approximately ₹15,000 per month. This reported income reflects his renewed engagement with livelihood activities; the information provided does not specify his earlier monthly earnings.
The Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts in Kolar demonstrates the value of accessible counselling, therapeutic interventions and family-based support for individuals affected by substance dependence. Such assistance can help beneficiaries strengthen their well-being and participate more confidently in family and economic life.
The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment supports rehabilitation and drug demand reduction interventions under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), including assistance through Integrated Rehabilitation Centres for Addicts.

title: MoSJE and Ministry of Defence Join Hands to Strengthen Welfare of Senior Citizens in Cantonment Areas Across The Country

New Day Care Centres to be Established in Cantonments; Existing Centres and Senior Citizen Homes to be Supported and Expanded under AVYAY

Youth from Cantonment Areas to Receive Training as Geriatric Caregivers; Partnership to Promote Dignified, Secure and Active Ageing through Better Care and Community Participation
date:

                16 NOV 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE) under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Directorate General Defence Estates (DGDE), Ministry of Defence, in the National Capital here today, to strengthen the welfare and well-being of senior citizens residing in Cantonment areas.
The MoU was signed in the presence of Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh and Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr. Virendra Kumar.
Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary, MoSJE, Shri Sudhansh Pant, Director General, Defence Estates, Smt. Shobha Gupta, Joint Secretary, MoSJE, Shri Sajeesh Kumar N, and other senior officers from both Ministries were present on the occasion.
The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was formally exchanged between Ms Kajal Singh, Director, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and Shri Mane AmitKumar B., Deputy Director General (Cantonments Division-II), Directorate General Defence Estates, Ministry of Defence, in the presence of the Union Ministers and senior officials of both Ministries.
Speaking at the event, Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar reaffirmed the Government's commitment under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, to ensuring dignified, secure and active ageing for every senior citizen.
Dr Kumar highlighted that through the Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana (AVYAY), the Ministry is supporting Senior Citizen Homes, Day Care Centres, Geriatric caregiver training, the National Helpline for Senior Citizens (
ELDERLINE – 14567
) and other welfare initiatives. He stated that the MoU would extend better care, welfare services and opportunities for active ageing to senior citizens living in Cantonment areas.
The Minister also appealed to citizens, particularly youth, officers and staff of Cantonment Boards and members of Cantonment communities, to register as
Vayo SAATHI
volunteers.
Launched on November 4, 2026, alongside the Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan, Vayo SAATHI encourages citizens aged 18 years and above to spend time with senior citizens, assist them in their daily needs and facilitate their access to welfare schemes, the Minister said.
Emphasising the importance of inter-generational companionship, Dr. Virendra Kumar said,
“Every Vayo SAATHI is a bridge between generations. I urge citizens to register as a Vayo SAATHI and become a companion to our elders.
”
Dr Kumar reiterated the Government’s commitment to the welfare of senior citizens and enumerated the initiatives taken by MoSJE, including the
Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana
(AVYAY), to improve the quality of life of the elderly.
He stated that the MoU marks an important step towards strengthening the support system for senior citizens residing in Cantonment areas by ensuring access to better care, welfare services and opportunities for active and dignified ageing.
Addressing the gathering, Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted that senior citizens are not merely members of families but also carriers of experience, traditions and social values. He observed that their guidance and wisdom would play an important role in the journey towards Viksit Bharat by 2047.
Shri Singh said their experience, wisdom and guidance will be invaluable in the journey to create peaceful, harmonious and knowledgeable societies.
Highlighting their lifelong contribution to building families, society and the nation, he termed it a social and moral responsibility to ensure that they are accorded respect, security and a sense of belonging.
Recalling the Indian ethos of
“Matru Devo Bhava, Pitru Devo Bhava”,
he emphasised that caring for senior citizens is a social and moral responsibility as well as a national duty, extending beyond the boundaries of individual families.
While acknowledging the progress made in senior citizen welfare, Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised the need for continuous improvement in the delivery of services to the elderly.
The Raksha Mantri also called for regular social audits of Day Care Centres and Senior Citizen Homes to assess the quality of services, identify areas requiring further improvement and address gaps through continuous monitoring.
In his closing remarks, Secretary, MoSJE, Shri Sudhansh Pant said that the MoU represents a shared commitment towards ensuring companionship, dignity and care for senior citizens closer to their homes.
Joint Secretary, MoSJE, Shri Sajeesh Kumar N, stated that a Joint Working Group would work closely with DGDE to ensure that the new Day Care Centres become operational and caregiver training programmes commence in the identified Cantonments at the earliest.
The MoU aims to promote the welfare of senior citizens residing in Cantonment areas under the Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana (AVYAY). The partnership envisages the establishment of new Day Care Centres and Senior Citizen Homes with residential facilities of 25/50-bed capacity, wherever feasible. It will also support and strengthen existing facilities run by Cantonment Boards.
Under the arrangement, DGDE will facilitate the provision of infrastructure, premises and basic civic amenities, while the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment will extend financial assistance, technical guidance, training and operational support.
The partnership will also focus on training youth from Cantonment areas as geriatric caregivers, along with awareness generation, skill development and promotion of inter-generational bonding. A Joint Working Group will be constituted to monitor implementation, facilitate coordination and ensure effective execution of the initiatives. The MoU will remain valid for five years, with a provision for renewal.
The MoU comes at a significant juncture as the Defence Estates Department marks its centenary, commemorating 100 years since its establishment in 1926. The partnership reflects the expanding role of the Defence Estates Department from administration to community welfare.
By bringing together the infrastructure and civic facilities of Cantonment Boards with the policy, technical and financial support of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, the initiative exemplifies the
Whole of Government
approach towards ensuring the welfare, dignity and well-being of senior citizens.

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment will organise the Departmental Summit
‘Samaveshi Niti Sankalp’
on November 18–19 (Wednesday & Thursday) at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan in the National Capital, as a significant step towards realising the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.
The Summit is the third in the series of Departmental Summits envisioned by the Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, to foster collective ownership of national priorities and accelerate development outcomes through closer collaboration between the Centre and the States.
Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, is scheduled to grace the Valedictory Session.
The two-day Summit aims to provide an institutional platform for meaningful dialogue, shared responsibility and coordinated action between the Union and State Governments on key policy priorities, programmes, initiatives and strategies for strengthening social justice and inclusive development.
Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice, Shri Sudhansh Pant said in preparation for the Summit, the Ministry has undertaken systematic consultations with field-level functionaries and stakeholders to ensure that ground-level experiences and implementation-related insights form policy deliberations.
He said a series of video conferences were held with State and Union Territory officials, while feedback was invited on four thematic areas from stakeholders within and outside the Government.
The consultation exercise received an overwhelming response, with more than 13,500 responses from over 450 districts, whileas these valuable inputs have been incorporated into the background notes prepared for the Summit, the Secretary said.
Shri Pant said the Departmental Summit model brings together political leadership and senior officials from the Union and State Governments to deliberate on important issues relating to the Ministry's mandate.
It provides an opportunity to share successful practices, address implementation challenges, explore innovative approaches and develop time-bound action plans to ensure effective implementation of government initiatives and delivery of their benefits to intended beneficiaries, he said.
The Secretary said the Summit will focus on four key thematic areas, namely,
‘Reimagining Prevention and Drug Demand Reduction Strategy for a Nasha Mukt Bharat’,
‘One Nation, One Scholarship Portal – Accessible Scholarships, Empowered Students’
,
‘Early Intervention and Reduction of Disability Burden’
and
‘Sugamya Bharat for Viksit Bharat’
.
These themes reflect the Ministry's commitment to strengthening social inclusion, enhancing access to welfare initiatives and promoting the empowerment of all sections of society, he added.
Giving the details, Shri Pant said the deliberations will be conducted through four breakout sessions and two full-house sessions, enabling comprehensive discussions on the identified themes.
All States and Union Territories will be provided dedicated opportunities to make presentations during the breakout sessions and share their views during the full-house sessions, Shri Pant said.
He added two experts will also share insights on international best practices to enrich the discussions and facilitate the adoption of innovative approaches for effective programme implementation.
As part of the Summit, delegates will visit a Digital Exhibition showcasing key initiatives and technological interventions of the Ministry, that will  feature integrated portals such as
‘Samavesh’
and
‘e-Anudan’
, mobile applications developed for field-level operations and success stories highlighting the impact of various schemes and programmes of the Ministry, the Secretary said.
Shri Pant noted the digital exhibition will provide an opportunity to showcase technology-driven interventions and innovative approaches supporting effective implementation and improved delivery of services to beneficiaries.
It will also highlight the Ministry's efforts towards strengthening institutional mechanisms and promoting inclusive development through digital platforms and field-level initiatives, he added.
The Secretary said the Summit is expected to facilitate meaningful exchange of ideas, promote mutual learning among States and Union Territories, and strengthen collaborative strategies for building an inclusive, equitable and empowered society.
Shri Pant informed that the key outcomes and action plans, along with defined timelines for their implementation, will be presented before the Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, during the valedictory session.
The Secretary noted the guidance of the Hon’ble Prime Minister will stimulate the collective resolve of the Centre and the States, providing  renewed impetus to the collective efforts and setting the course for decisive, coordinated and time-bound action towards achieving the agreed outcomes  and advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

title: PRESS NOTE ON PERIODIC LABOUR FORCE SURVEY (PLFS) MONTHLY BULLETIN October, 2026
subtitle:
Female labour force and workforce participation increased

Urban UR declined
date:

content:
Snapshot:
Overall LFPR (15+ years) increased to 55.7% in October, 2026, a rise of 0.3 percentage points year-on-year.
Rural LFPR (15+ years) improved to 58.4% in October, 2026, gaining 0.4 percentage points over the past month and 0.6 percentage points over the year.
Overall female LFPR (15+ years) recorded an increase of 0.8 percentage points year-on-year to 35.0% in October, 2026.
Overall WPR (15+ years) improved by 0.5 percentage points year-on-year to 53.0%.
Female WPR (15+ years) recorded at 33.3% an increase of 0.5 percentage points over last month.
Overall UR (15+ years) decreased to 4.9% in October, 2026, 0.3 percentage points lower than a year earlier.
Overall female UR fell by 0.4 percentage points year-on-year to 5.0%, with rural female UR dropping to 3.8%, its lowest level recorded during 2026.
A.        Introduction
The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by NSO, MoSPI, is the primary source of data on activity participation and employment and unemployment conditions of the population. The PLFS survey methodology has been modified from January, 2025 to provide monthly and quarterly estimates of labour force indicators for the country.
Monthly results of PLFS are released in the form of Monthly Bulletins. It presents estimates of key labour market indicators
viz.
Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR) at the all-India level following the Current Weekly Status
[1]
(CWS) approach.
The Monthly Bulletins for April, 2025 to September, 2026 have already been released. The present Monthly Bulletin for October, 2026 is the nineteenth in the series.
Key findings for persons of age 15 years and above following CWS:
Rural areas lead the improvement in labour force participation:
The overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) for persons aged 15 years and above improved marginally to 55.7% in October, 2026, compared to 55.5% in September, 2026. In rural areas, LFPR increased from 58.0% to 58.4% over the month, while the urban LFPR stood at 50.5% in October, 2026 against 50.7% in September, 2026.
On a year-on-year basis, the overall LFPR improved by 0.3 percentage points, increasing from 55.4% in October, 2025 to 55.7% in October, 2026. During the same period, rural areas recorded a gain of 0.6 percentage points, with rural LFPR increasing from 57.8% to 58.4%, while urban LFPR remained unchanged at 50.5%.
Overall LFPR reached 55.7% in October, 2026, showing an improvement over both the preceding month and the corresponding month a year earlier.
Overall Female Labour Force Participation increased:
Overall female LFPR improved to 35.0% in October, 2026 from 34.6% in September, 2026, making its highest level since February, 2026. Rural female LFPR rose by 0.6 percentage points over the month and reached 39.5% in October, 2026. However, female LFPR in urban areas remained stable at 25.9%.
Over the year, the overall female LFPR increased by 0.8 percentage points, from 34.2% in October, 2025 to 35.0% in October, 2026. Rural female LFPR gained 1.1 percentage points, rising from 38.4% to 39.5% and urban female LFPR gained 0.5 percentage points, from 25.4% to 25.9% during the same period.
Female LFPR increased in both rural and urban areas on a year-on-year basis, reaching 39.5% and 25.9%, respectively, in October, 2026.
Workforce participation witnessed improvement
:
Overall WPR increased to 53.0% in October, 2026 from 52.7% in September, 2026, reaching its highest level since February, 2026. Rural WPR increased by 0.5 percentage points over the previous month to 56.0% in October, 2026, whereas urban WPR remained broadly stable at 47.1%.
Among male, WPR remained largely unchanged at 73.7% in October, 2026, against 73.6% in September, 2026. In rural areas, male WPR rose to 75.3% from 74.9% during the same period. Female WPR recorded a more notable month-on-month improvement, increasing from 32.8% in September, 2026 to 33.3% in October, 2026. This was supported by increase in both rural and urban areas, with female WPR rising from 37.4% to 38.0% in rural areas and from 23.5% to 23.7% in urban areas.
On a year-on-year basis, overall WPR expanded from 52.5% in October, 2025 to 53.0% in October, 2026, marking a 0.5 percentage point improvement. Rural WPR recorded an increase of 0.8 percentage points, from 55.2% to 56.0% in October, 2026 compared to the previous year, while urban WPR remained broadly stable at 47.1% in October, 2026 compared to 47.0% a year back.
Overall female WPR increased by 0.9 percentage points year-on-year to 33.3% in October, 2026, with increases recorded in both rural and urban areas.
Urban Unemployment Rate (UR) improved:
The overall Unemployment Rate (UR) among persons aged 15 years and above decreased to 4.9% in October, 2026, from 5.0% in September, 2026. Compared with the previous month, rural UR remained steady at 4.2%, while urban UR declined by 0.2 percentage points, from 6.9% to 6.7% in October, 2026.
Compared with the corresponding month of 2025
, the overall UR declined by 0.3 percentage points, from 5.2% to 4.9% in October, 2026. During the same period, rural UR declined by 0.2 percentage points, from 4.4% to 4.2% and urban UR declined by 0.3 percentage points, from 7.0% to 6.7%.
Overall UR stood at 4.9% in October, 2026, lower by 0.3 percentage points compared to a year earlier.
.
Female UR declined:
The overall and urban male UR among persons aged 15 years and above remained unchanged at 4.9% and 6.0%, respectively, in October, 2026, as in the previous month. Over the last month, rural male UR stood at 4.3% in October, 2026 from 4.4% in September, 2026. Among female, the overall UR declined to 5.0% in October, 2026, compared with 5.2% in September, 2026. Rural female UR estimated at 3.8 % in October, 2026, against 3.9% in the previous month while urban female UR recorded at 8.7% in October, 2026, against 9.2% in the previous month.
On a year-on-year basis, the overall male UR declined by 0.2 percentage points, from 5.1% in October, 2025 to 4.9% in October, 2026. The improvement was more pronounced in rural areas, where male UR fell by 0.3 percentage points, from 4.6% to 4.3%, while urban male UR remained broadly stable at 6.0% in October, 2026. Overall female UR decreased by 0.4 percentage points to 5.0% from 5.4% in the previous year. UR for rural female declined by 0.2 percentage points from 4.0% in October, 2025 to 3.8% in October, 2026. In urban areas, female UR fell by 1.0% points to 8.7% in October, 2026 from 9.7% observed in the previous year.
Female UR declined in both rural and urban areas, while rural female UR recorded its lowest level of 2026 at 3.8%.
